Synthese maken: De resultaten en inzichten van een brede, verkennende probleemanalyse combineren, op basis daarvan het probleem herformuleren en specificeren, en vervolgens rapporteren aan een probleemeigenaar of opdrachtgever in de vorm van een kort beleidsadvies of 'policy brief';

Reflecteren op mogelijke rollen van een beleidsanalist en voor concrete situaties beargumenteren welke rol(len) een beleidsanalist zinvol kan spelen, ter ondersteuning van een bestaande probleemeigenaar met een bestaand TB-probleem.

Deze leerdoelen dragen bij aan de eindtermen van de opleiding Technische Bestuurskunde, en met name kennis en vaardigheden betreffende

de wetenschappelijke discipline 'beleidsanalyse'

analyseren

rekening houden met de temporele en maatschappelijke context

wetenschappelijke benadering

intellectuele basisvaardigheden

bekwaam in samenwerken en communiceren

description:
In het vak ‘Ethiek en Veiligheid’ leer je de basisconcepten en -methoden van a) Wetenschapsfilosofie en Ethiek en b) Veiligheidswetenschappen (Safety & Security), en leer je beide wetenschapsdomeinen met elkaar te verbinden. Het vertalen van deze kennis in de praktijk is een belangrijk onderdeel van dit vak.

Het vak start met Wetenschapsfilosofie, waarbij onder meer de volgende vragen aan bod komen: Wat is wetenschap? Wat maakt wetenschappelijke kennis waardevol? Welke rol speelt de persoonlijke achtergrond van wetenschappers in de vergaring van wetenschappelijke kennis? Welke invloed hebben methodologische keuzes (bijvoorbeeld keuzes over kwantitatief versus kwalitatief onderzoek) op wetenschappelijke bevindingen? Hebben wetenschappers een ethisch-maatschappelijke verantwoordelijkheid in de uitvoering van hun onderzoek?  Wat is de relatie tussen wetenschappelijke kennis en macht?

Wat betreft veiligheid maak je kennis met belangrijke theorieën, modellen en methoden van risicomanagement. Deze veiligheidsconcepten en -methoden zullen verankerd worden met normatieve ethische reflecties. Welke ethische kwesties komen bijvoorbeeld aan bod tijdens het maken van beslissingen over risicoanalyse methoden? En welke normatieve beslissingen worden meegenomen in risicomanagement? Studenten leren ethische kwesties op vlak van veiligheid herkennen en interpreteren, en leren om filosofische benaderingen in te zetten om na te gaan welke ethische aspecten zich voordoen tijdens onderzoek en technologiebeleid en -beheer.

Hoe is dit vak verbonden met de TB-opleiding? In de eindtermen van de opleiding is opgenomen dat een TB-bachelor een wetenschappelijke benadering heeft. In dit vak leer je over de ‘wetenschappelijke benadering’ en leer je kritsch te reflecteren op je eigen positie en verantwoordelijkheid als wetenschapper en de betekenis die verschillende wetenschappelijke methodes met zich meebrengen. Een andere eindterm is dat TB-studenten kunnen reflecteren op ethische en morele vraagstukken waar de wetenschap tegenaan loopt. Ook aan het behalen van dit leerdoel besteedt dit vak veel aandacht. Veiligheidswetenschappen is het toepassingsgebied dat is gekozen in dit vak. De reden is dat in alle drie de technische specialisaties (maar ook in technische domeinen daarbuiten) veiligheid een zeer belangrijk criterium is waarop bestaande en nieuwe technologieën worden beoordeeld.

Bovendien kan dit vak gezien worden als een belangrijke voorbereiding voor je bachelor-eindproject (BEP). Je leert een onderzoeksvraag uitwerken op basis van een probleemstelling, je leert onderbouwde keuzes maken voor onderzoeksmethoden, je gaat aan de slag met het toepassen van de gekozen onderzoeksmethoden (op kleine schaal), en je reflecteert over de onderzoeksresultaten en het onderzoeksproces.
learning_objectives:
Je kan kritisch reflecteren op de (maatschappelijke) betekenis van wetenschappelijk onderzoek, de implicaties van het kiezen voor verschillende methodes, de positie en verantwoordelijkheid van onderzoekers, en de macht van wetenschap.

Je kan morele argumenten evalueren

Je kan waarden identificeren en normatieve ethische reflecties in veiligheidswetenschappen toepassen

Je kan een probleemstelling identificeren gebaseerd op wetenschappelijke literatuur, en dit vertalen in een onderzoeksvraag

Je kan een onderbouwde keuze maken in basismethoden in het domein van veiligheidswetenschappen, en kan deze methoden in de praktijk toepassen

Je kan samenwerken in team, en een onderzoeksrapport schrijven

description: De module behandelt de theorie en de praktijk van het kiezen en implementeren van geschikte vormen van economische coördinatie in het ontwerpen, aanleggen en beheren van infrastructuren. Voorbeelden van belangrijke aspecten hierbij zijn de keus tussen publiek, privaat of collectief eigendom, contractvormen en tariefstructuren, samenwerkingsvormen, overheidssturing en vormen van toezicht en regulering. Hierbij wordt gebruik gemaakt van neo-klassieke en institutioneel economische theorie.
learning_objectives:
Het kunnen beschrijven van de belangrijkste vraagstukken op het gebied van economie van infrastructuren, met een focus op netgebonden systemen voor energie en watervoorziening, communicatie en transport.

Het kunnen beschrijven van de verschillen tussen de neo-klassieke, de nieuw institutionele en de origineel institutionele economie, aan de hand van de onderliggende assumpties, de specifieke theorieen en de relevante methode van analyse.

Het aan de hand van die verschillen kunnen beoordelen wat de relevante economische leerstukken en concepten zijn om specifieke infrastructurele vraagstukken te kunnen analyseren.

Het kunnen identificeren, beschrijven en interpreteren van deze vraagstukken, met gebruikmaking van leerstukken en concepten van de drie verschillende economische scholen.

Het kritisch kunnen reflecteren op overheidsbeleid en bedrijfsmangement rond infrastructuren.

Het kunnen identificeren van de aard van problemen in overheidsbeleid en bedrijfsmanagement rond infrastructuren, in het licht van maatschappelijke en technologische veranderingen.

description:
Centrale vraag in dit vak is hoe besluiten en sturing tot stand komen bij belangrijke publieke vraagstukken. We onderscheiden daarbij juridische en bestuurlijke overwegingen en werken die uit. Daarbij veronderstellen we dat zowel juridische als bestuurlijke overwegingen van belang zijn, maar ook strijdig kunnen zijn.

De kennis wordt toegepast op zowel intra- als inter-organisatorische processen. Die kunnen onderling verschillen, maar ook belangrijke overeenkomsten vertonen. Het vak is tevens een verkenning van die overeenkomsten en verschillen.

In het bestuur-onderdeel worden theorieën behandeld over sturing en gedrag in complexe netwerken, zowel binnen als tussen organisaties. In het recht-onderdeel van dit vak wordt op de juridische vraagstukken die hierbij aan de orde zijn ingegaan.

In dit vak leer je hoe je een kwalitatief onderzoek kunt uitvoeren met behulp van de case study-methodologie. Daarnaast staan de vaardigheden teamwork en interviewen centraal in het vak.

Het is belangrijk om als toekomstig TB-ingenieur enige kennis te hebben van kwalitatieve data-analyse en conceptueel modelleren. TB-ingenieurs werken aan complexe maatschappelijke vraagstukken, waarbij technische modellen en kwantitatieve data belangrijk maar niet afdoende zijn. Niet alle aspecten van een probleem of vraagstuk zijn immers (direct) in cijfers te vangen. Bij het duiden van de context, menselijke ervaringen of het in kaart brengen van oorzaak-gevolg relaties speelt kwalitatieve data vaak een cruciale rol. Kwalitatief onderzoek helpt dan om complexe situaties beter te begrijpen en levert belangrijke kennis voor het ontwerpen of implementeren van technologie.

Als je bijvoorbeeld wilt begrijpen waarom een innovatieve technologie (denk bijvoorbeeld aan een waterstofauto) niet goed van de grond komt, is het niet genoeg om alleen naar technische prestaties of marktdata te kijken. Je moet ook weten hoe gebruikers de technologie ervaren, welke rol wet- en regelgeving spelen, hoe partijen in de keten samenwerken en waar weerstand of misverstanden ontstaan.

Gedurende het vak voer je in een groep een kwalitatief onderzoek uit rondom een specifieke casus. Je doorloop je de volledige onderzoekscyclus en past kennis toe uit eerdere vakken in de leerlijn (= BRO1 en BRO2). Je werkt met twee 'klassieke' kwalitatieve methoden, namelijk interviews en documentanalyse. Daarnaast pas je een andere, meer creatieve methode naar keuze toe.

Tijdens hoorcolleges nemen we je mee in de basisprincipes van wetenschapsfilosofie, verkennen we de verschillen tussen kwantitatief en kwalitatief onderzoek en laten we zien hoe dit type onderzoek past binnen TB. In de werkcolleges werk je aan het onderzoeksvoorstel, je maakt kennis met de verschillende onderzoeksmethoden en past ze toe op jouw onderzoek. Daarnaast leer je hoe je effectief kunt samenwerken als onderzoeksteam en werk je aan je vaardigheden als interviewer.
learning_objectives:
Na afronding van dit vak kun je:

De kenmerken en het doel van wetenschappelijk onderzoek begrijpen en onderscheiden van probleemoplossing en modelleren.

De uitgangspunten en achtergronden van kwalitatief onderzoek verklaren en vergelijken met kwantitatieve methoden.

Een theoretische, methodologische en empirische ambitie formuleren voor kwalitatief onderzoek.

Zelfstandig een case study-onderzoek uitvoeren, door middel van:

Toepassing van een concept, theorie of model uit de BRO-leerlijn.

Het opstellen en uitvoeren van een plan voor de selectie, verzameling en analyse van geschikte informatie ter beantwoording van een kwalitatieve onderzoeksvraag.

Het combineren van verschillende kwalitatieve onderzoeksmethoden, waaronder documentanalyse, interviews en een creatieve onderzoekstechniek.

Reflecteren op de keuzes binnen het onderzoeksproces en het expliciteren van de invloed van theoretische kaders en persoonlijke interpretaties.

description: In Systeemmodelleren 3 - Simulatiemethoden worden 2 verschillende simulatiemethoden onderwezen: Agent-Based Modelling (ABM) en System Dynamics (SD). Er ligt relatief veel nadruk op het zelf oefenen met het conceptualiseren, formuleren, evalueren en gebruiken van modellen, waarbij de theorie dient om studenten op gang te helpen en om verschillende concepten en de achtergrond van de twee modelleermethoden beter te begrijpen.

Beleidsgericht empirisch onderzoek heeft als doel om nieuwe kennis te vergaren welke als basis kan dienen voor de ontwikkeling van effectief beleid. Binnen dit vak leer je om dergelijk onderzoek op te zetten, uit te voeren en te rapporteren. Het vak is opgebouwd rond de vier fasen/onderdelen van het onderzoeksproces:

(1) het formuleren van het probleem en de doel- en vraagstelling van het onderzoek,

(2) de literatuurverkenning en het conceptuele model,

(3) de operationalisatie en dataverzameling,

(4) de data-analyse en interpretatie en de formulering van conclusies, aanbevelingen en beperkingen.

Aan de hand van specifieke casussen uit de verschillende domeinen (ICT, transport en energie) zal geoefend worden met het doorlopen van deze onderzoeksfasen. Uiteindelijk is het doel om op basis van de inzichten die voortkomen uit het onderzoek concrete beleidsaanbevelingen te formuleren.
learning_objectives:
Per fase van het onderzoek zijn de volgende specifieke leerdoelen geformuleerd:

(1) Formuleren van het probleem en de doel- en vraagstelling van het onderzoek. Na deze cursus kun je:

1. een overtuigende probleemformulering opstellen.

2. van een probleemformulering logisch redeneren naar een relevant onderzoeksdoel en gerelateerde onderzoeksvraag.

3. gegeven een onderzoeksvraag een geschikte onderzoeksmethode kiezen en motiveren.

4. reflecteren op een onderzoeksmethode in termen van interne validiteit (causaliteit) en ecologische validiteit.

(2) Literatuurverkenning en conceptueel model. Na deze cursus kun je:

5. kritisch reflecteren op bestaand wetenschappelijk onderzoek.

6. wetenschappelijke literatuur verwerken in een overtuigend verhaal met als doel om relevante kennislacunes te identificeren.

7. een conceptueel model opstellen (begrippen definiëren en relaties onderbouwen).

8. vaststellen of bepaalde relaties aan de 4 voorwaarden van causaliteit voldoen.

(3) Operationaliseren en data verzamelen. Na deze cursus kun je:

9. begrippen operationaliseren (enquêtevragen opstellen).

10. een samengestelde schaal opstellen en de validiteit en betrouwbaarheid van de geconstrueerde schaal empirisch controleren.

11. gegeven een onderzoeksdoel, de populatie van een onderzoek definiëren.

12. op basis van de definitie van de populatie, een geschikte methode van steekproeftrekking kiezen en motiveren.

13. een representativiteitsanalyse uitvoeren en hieruit relevante implicaties voor het onderzoek formuleren.

(4) Data analyseren, resultaten interpreteren en formuleren van conclusies, aanbevelingen en beperkingen. Na deze cursus kun je:

14. multivariate data-analyse technieken toepassen en de resultaten daarvan interpreteren.

15. analyseresultaten verwerken in overzichtelijke tabellen.

16. schijn- en onderdrukte relaties herkennen op basis van modelresultaten.

17. aan de hand van de resultaten van een onderzoek relevante conclusies trekken en aanbevelingen formuleren.

18. reflecteren op de beperkingen van een onderzoek en mogelijkheden voor vervolgonderzoek identificeren.

description:
Dit projectvak wordt hoofdzakelijk uitgevoerd door groepjes van twee studenten. Elk groepje krijgt: (1) een modelleermethode toegewezen volgens de capaciteit die daarvoor is, systeemdynamica (SD) of agent-gebaseerd modelleren (ABM), en (2) een socio-technisch probleem dat zij kwantitatief gaan modelleren. Groepen die willen wisselen van modelleermethode kunnen onderling ruilen, binnen de beschikbare capaciteit. Studenten vormen een beleidsanalyse uit op het socio-technische probleem.

Elk groepje doorloopt de gehele modelleercyclus. Vervolgens wordt het model gebruikt om een onderzoeksvraag/probleem te analyseren en te rapporteren in een wetenschappelijk artikel.

Parallel aan het modelleren en simuleren zal de academische schrijfvaardigheid worden verbeterd middels schrijfopdrachten en werkcolleges. De schrijfvaardigheid in het zelfgeschreven wetenschappelijke artikel wordt expliciet getoetst.

In de modelleerpractica zullen er peer reviews plaatsvinden in week 3 en peer grading in week 7. In de schrijfvaardigheidscolleges zullen er twee feedback momenten zijn op een stuk van maximaal 500 woorden. (Dit is een voorlopige planning).
learning_objectives:
Na het volgen van dit vak kan de student:

- met systeem dynamische of agent-gebaseerde software een kwantitatief model van een socio-technisch probleem ontwikkelen volgens de modelleringscyclus.

- conclusies en aanbevelingen afleiden uit een modelgebaseerde analyse van een complex social-technisch probleem.

- de gekozen probleemfocus, conceptualisering, modelformalisering, evaluatie en bevindingen wetenschappelijke rapporteren en illustreren, afgestemd op de virtuele probleemeigenaar/doelgroep en houdend aan de geldende schrijfconventies

description: Dit vak behandelt de modellering van technische systemen in de energiesector en de industrie op basis van het vakgebied van de fysische transportverschijnselen (warmte-, stof- en impulsoverdracht).

This course deepens your skills and conceptual understanding of programming. You will learn object- oriented Design (OOD) with UML and Object-Oriented Programming (OOP) with Java. UML and Java are industry standard design and programming languages used to develop enterprise software, desktop apps, web apps, mobile apps, games and much more. In this course, you will learn how to position the languages you learned so far, and what to use when: Low-code (TB141Ic), scripting (TB133d; TB142Ic) and object-oriented (TB241Ib). You will also familiarize yourself with Java development tools and practices that allow you to write clean and reusable code and to understand and modify existing ones easily. The skill set you will earn in this course can be useful, in the future, to design and build software tools and components, to update or upscale software, or to manage a java project.
learning_objectives:
At the end of this course, you will be able to:

LO1 - Identify key characteristics of the Java programming language and development environment (EDI, SDK, JVM, etc.)

LO2 - Use basic Java APIs and components (data types, data structures, algorithmic structures, and methods)

LO3 - Apply key elements, concepts, and design patterns of object-oriented programming

LO4 - Write clean, understandable, and reusable code following Java coding best practices

LO5 - Develop object-oriented programs using Java.

description:
According to the Council of Supply Chain Management Professionals logistics is defined as "the process of planning, implementing, and controlling procedures for the efficient and effective transportation and storage of goods including services, and related information from the point of origin to the point of consumption for the purpose of conforming to customer requirements."

Logistics activities should be in line with other business activities such as marketing and purchasing, in order to create sustainable competitive advantages for individual companies and service providers, and for the supply chain as a whole. Given the strategic importance of logistics for individual organizations and supply chains, it is vital to know how the performance of logistics activities is measured, and how these activities can be modelled and improved.

Therefore in this course different logistics aspects are discussed and analyzed. A selection of quantitative methodologies are introduced to model and provide solutions to a wide range of relevant problems in logistics.

We focus on two classes of logistics problems:

Logistics problems within organizations: forecasting and demand modeling; inventory management; clustering and classification of items.

Distribution problems.

Methodologies include analytical models, linear programming models, basic data mining techniques.

De thermodynamica van energieprocessen (fase- en toestandsdiagrammen, kringprocessen, exergieanalyse) en de werking en prestatie van (onderdelen van) elektriciteitscentrales, warmtepompen, brandstofcellen en installaties voor zonne-energie.
learning_objectives:
- fasediagrammen, toestandsdiagrammen en kringprocessen kunnen tekenen en interpreteren
- de werking van verschillende types elektriciteitscentrales, brandstofcellen en warmtepompen kunnen uitleggen en het rendement (van onderdelen) daarvan kunnen definiëren en berekenen
- kunnen uitleggen wat exergie en exergieverlies is en exergieverliezen, -waardes en -rendementen kunnen berekenen
- de werking en prestatie van PV-cellen kunnen uitleggen resp. berekenen, en rendement en terugverdientijd van CSP en zonneboiler kunnen berekenen
- een model kunnen maken in en berekeningen kunnen uitvoeren met het flowsheetprogramma Cycle-Tempo

description: Internet is a global system that has interconnected various kinds of systems and services worldwide. This course analyzes the architecture and core technologies of the Internet from systemic and interdisciplinary perspectives. As a hands-on oriented course, we learn network programming (using python) and apply the learned programming skills in practical settings. Attention is paid to the increasing importance of interconnected environments, in particular the networking of engineering systems and services through digital platforms. We analyse the concept of interconnected engineering systems on the basis of concrete cases, e.g., connected cars, cyber-physical systems, as means to illustrate the complex interactions of technology and society. In addition, a number of modern development and research themes will be discussed for the evolution of distributed information and communication systems, e.g., new networking and computing techniques for large-scale deployment of the Internet of Things (IoT). On top of the key technologies, we consider the social context to which the high expectations of the future Internet technologies need to tackle in terms of security, privacy risks.
learning_objectives:
After the course, students are able to:

- Illustrate Internet architecture, design principles and routing algorithms

- Evaluate computing paradigms and wireless and mobile communication in practical scenarios

- Design networking programming solutions for practical problems

- Apply Internet of Things (IoT) and cyber-physical systems (CPS) technologies in case studies

- Analyze security and privacy risks, challenges and solutions for interconnected engineering systems such as IoT

description: Het transportsysteem levert enorme maatschappelijke voordelen op. Daarnaast leidt het systeem ook tot maatschappelijke problemen: verkeersonveiligheid, milieuschade en files om de meest in het oog springende problemen te noemen. De overheid neemt veel maatregelen om het transportsysteem te verbeteren. In dit vak leer je welke beleidsmaatregelen mogelijk tot verbeteringen zouden kunnen leiden. Het vak is een vervolg op het eerstejaarsvak: "Analyse van het transportsysteem". In dit eerstejaarsvak heb je geleerd de effecten van beleidsmaatregelen kwantitatief te schatten. In dit tweedejaarsvak leer je om de kwantitatieve effecten te waarderen met een maatschappelijke kosten-batenanalyse om zodoende de netto contante waarde (en kosten-batenratio) van een beleidsmaatregel te kunnen schatten

Summary

The course is designed to provide students with a comprehensive understanding of large-scale production processes, ranging from individual unit operations to the level of integrated industrial clusters. Students will learn to identify the fundamental components of a process flowsheet, understand their functions, sequencing, and interconnections, and carry out relevant engineering calculations.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, you should be able to:

- Identify and name the feedstock, unit operations, and products of selected industrial production processes

- Describe the processing steps, required unit operations, and product chains of selected industrial production processes

- Explain the basic functioning of reactors and separation units

- Calculate the performance of simple production processes through mass balances

- Calculate the performance of reactors and separation units

description:
This module is about assessing and overcoming risks in ICT to ensure systems are maintainable in the long term in complex multi-actor environments and that they do not create new risks. You learn to understand the different hardware components that make up ICT systems and the different organisational, inter-organisational and large-scale systems designs. You learn how to use this knowledge to assess the risks different ICT systems pose for individuals, organisations and society. You will also learn the different strategies to reduce these risks and determine if and how to apply them.

The theoretical background will be explained during the course during different lectures and guest lectures. In different groups, you will then apply the theory to several cases in which you will assess risks and identify strategies for reducing them. You will present your case to the other students in the course, after which they can ask questions about it, and there will be a more in-depth discussion of the case, the strategies chosen, and the considerations made.
learning_objectives:
- To explain the hardware components of ICT systems (network devices, servers, workstations).

- To compare different designs for organisational, inter-organisational and large-scale systems.

- To propose different hardware and management strategies for reducing risks in ICT.

- To estimate the risks of ICT systems on the system's level, within organisations and on an inter-organisational and societal level.

- To assess the risks of an ICT system on the system's level, within organisations and on an inter-organisational and societal level in a given case.

- To recommend an appropriate strategy for reducing risks for an ICT system in a given case.

description: In dit vak wordt de governance van het energie- en industriedomein behandeld: hoe de actoren (zoals marktpartijen, netwerkbeheerders, consumenten en overheidsorganen) samen voor een efficiënte, duurzame en betrouwbare energievoorziening kunnen zorgen. Het belangrijkste leerstuk in dit vak is samenhang tussen (i) de inrichting van de elektriciteits-, waterstof-, gas- en warmtesystemen en -markten en (ii) de techno-economische karakteristieken van die sectoren. We bestuderen ook de governance van complexe industrieclusters. Studenten dienen de voor- en nadelen van verschillende governanceopties kunnen analyseren en veranderingen ervan kunnen beoordelen.

Hoofddoel: Na afloop van dit vak ben je in staat om te evalueren en bediscussiëren hoe de sturing van data geproduceerd, verzameld, gedeeld, verwerkt en (her)gebruikt door verschillende actoren in verschillende contexten in onze huidige informatiemaatschappij kan plaatsvinden.

Visie: Technologische ontwikkelingen hebben het voor verschillende actoren mogelijk gemaakt om op grote schaal data te verzamelen, creëren, verwerken en gebruiken. In eerdere I&C-vakken heb je je al verdiept in zulke technologische ontwikkelingen (bijvoorbeeld datawarehouses, Internet of Things, en informatiearchitecturen).

Het verzamelen, creëren, delen en hergebruik van data heeft zowel voor- als nadelen en vindt op verschillende niveaus plaats: internationaal, nationaal en lokaal. Op alle niveaus en binnen alle actorgroepen interacteren veel verschillende actoren. In dit vak gaan we hier verder op in. Ook gaan we kijken naar publieke belangen die een rol spelen in de context van dit vak, zoals rechtsgelijkheid, economische groei en transparantie. Daarnaast gaan we in op verschillende vormen van falen (o.a. markt- en systeemfalen) die sturing noodzakelijk maken.

In dit vak zullen we governance met name aan de hand van cases behandelen, waaronder governance op het gebied van open data, privacy en AI. We gaan kijken hoe sturingsarrangementen die door overheidsorganisaties en andere actoren kunnen worden ingezet publieke belangen borgen of juist aantasten. Ook gaan we binnen de cases kijken naar hoe deze sturingsarrangementen vormen van falen, waarom markt- en systeemfalen, kunnen tegengaan. Deze cases zijn gekozen omdat ze laten zien hoe governance op verschillende niveaus en in verschillende contexten kan plaatsvinden.

Een breed scala aan actoren in de transportmarkt (zowel private partijen als overheidsorganen) probeert samen belangrijke producten en diensten (havens, wegen, openbaar vervoer, bereikbaarheid) voor de maatschappij te leveren zonder dat dit ten koste gaat van een schoon milieu, verkeersonveiligheid of van gezonde overheidsfinanciën. Governance gaat over processen, gewoontes, beleid, wetten en regels die van betekenis zijn voor de manier waarop mensen een markt (in dit geval de transportmarkt) sturen, besturen, beheren en controleren. Het belangrijkste leerstuk in dit vak is dat studenten vooral de rol van de overheid begrijpen in het besturen en beheren van de transportmarkt, dat ze kunnen analyseren hoe transportbeleid tot stand komen, dat ze beleid kunnen analyseren op voor-en nadelen, en dat ze met beleidsideeën kunnen komen waarbij ze kunnen onderbouwen (op papier maar ook in een debat) of een aanpassing een verbetering of verslechtering is.

Dit vaak gaat over de governance van socio-technische systemen (STS). Governance definiëren we breed: all processes of governing, whether undertaken by a government, market, or network, whether through laws, power, contracts, norms or language (gebaseerd op Bevir, 2012:4). Hoewel technologie hier een belangrijke rol speelt, richt dit vak zich daarmee vooral op de interactie tussen technologie en de sociale elementen van STS, en in het bijzonder de manier waarop deze worden bestuurd.

Dit besturen is niet eenvoudig, gegeven de huidige uitdagingen waar overheden (bijv. ministeries, toezichthouders), bedrijven (en hun brancheorganisaties), en nonprofits en (samenwerkingsverbanden van) burgers vandaag de dag voor staan. Denk aan technologische innovaties, een geglobaliseerde economie, liberalisering en privatisering, demografische veranderingen, Europeanisering, etc.

Al deze ontwikkelingen maken governance zoals we het nu kennen: een complexe mix van hiërarchie-, markt- en netwerkelementen. Het is belangrijk om te weten hoe deze complexe mix werkt, want uiteindelijk worden de socio-technische systemen er door bestuurd.

In dit vak ga je aan de slag als sociaal-wetenschappelijk onderzoeker. Met behulp van kwalitatieve onderzoeksmethoden bestudeer je deze genoemde complexe mix. Met andere woorden: je neemt de governance van een STS als onderzoeksobject. Hoe werkt het? En waarom? De antwoorden op deze vragen zijn nodig om uiteindelijk te bekijken hoe tot effectieve en legitieme governance van STS kan worden gekomen.
learning_objectives:
Na succesvolle afronding van het vak, ben je in staat om

a) Theoretisch en conceptueel:

- De governance van STS te beschrijven aan de hand van de aangereikte concepten en dimensies

- De belangrijkste uitdagingen voor overheden, bedrijven, nonprofits en burgers en spanningsvelden in relatie tot de governance van STS te benoemen

- Te verklaren waarom de governance van STS op een bepaalde manier plaatsvindt of zich op een bepaalde manier ontwikkelt aan de hand van besproken mechanismen en condities

b) Methodologisch en onderzoekstechnisch:

- In het vak verworven theoretische en conceptuele kennis en inzichten toe te passen op een concreet governance vraagstuk

- Probleemstelling en vraagstelling voor een beschrijvend en verklarend wetenschappelijk onderzoek te formuleren

- Zelfstandig relevante wetenschappelijke literatuur te zoeken, te analyseren en te synthetiseren

- De case study methode op juiste wijze te gebruiken voor kwalitatief onderzoek

- Het gebruikmaken van een wetenschapscommunicatiemiddel om de inzichten het onderzoek door te vertalen naar een breder publiek.

course_name: Performance Analysis in Energy and Industry
description:
Analyse van actoren en prestatiecriteria van energie- en industriële systemen.

Project voor het analyseren en optimaliseren van een energie- of industrieel netwerk-systeem.

Lineair programmeren voor het optimaliseren van energie- en industriële systemen m.b.t. diverse prestatiecriteria.

Netwerkanalyse voor het analyseren en ontwerpen van energie- en industriële netwerken m.b.t. diverse prestatiecriteria.
learning_objectives: De student kan m.b.v. netwerkanalyse en procesoptimalisatie op verschillende systeemniveaus energie en industriële systemen analyseren, vergelijken en optimaliseren m.b.t. diverse relevante prestatiecriteria op het gebied van economie, milieu en betrouwbaarheid.

description:
Hoe ontwerp je een datagedreven systeem dat waarde oplevert voor alle betrokken partijen?

Denk aan een AI-systeem dat leert van patiëntdata. Moeten die data centraal worden opgeslagen, of blijven ze beter lokaal bij zorgaanbieders? Hoe houd je bij welke patiënten toestemming hebben gegeven voor het gebruik van hun data, zonder nieuwe privacyrisico’s te creëren? En wat voor businessmodellen passen bij zulke datagedreven toepassingen?

In dit vak onderzoek je dit soort vragen aan de hand van een complexe casus, waarin zowel AI (voor datagebruik) als blockchain (voor datatoegang) een rol spelen. Denk bijvoorbeeld aan slimme recyclingsystemen of medische besluitondersteuning.

Je krijgt nieuwe modelleerbenaderingen aangereikt om datagedreven architecturen te analyseren en ontwerpen:

Waardenetwerkanalyse en businessmodellen om de waardecreatie te begrijpen,

Enterprise-architectuurmodellen (zoals ArchiMate) om technische ontwerpkeuzes inzichtelijk te maken (bijv. centraal vs. decentraal).

Deze modellen gebruik je in een project om verschillende architectuurvarianten te ontwerpen, af te wegen en te onderbouwen. Je past je eerdere kennis uit vakken over data science en I&C-technologie toe, en verdiept je in de maatschappelijke impact van zulke systemen.

Je leert niet alleen hoe I&C bijdraagt aan maatschappelijke oplossingen, maar ook hoe je omgaat met ethische, privacy- en veiligheidsvraagstukken – voortbouwend op je kennis van I&C-risicobeheer (bijv. TB243I).
learning_objectives:
Na dit vak kun je:

1. Analyseren hoe I&C-technologieën waarde kunnen toevoegen aan maatschappelijke problemen, en afwegingen maken bij hun toepassing. Specifiek:

- Identificeren voor welke maatschappelijke problemen een IenC-technologie waarde kan toevoegen

- De implicaties beoordelen van een grootschalige IenC-implementatie in een maatschappelijke context

2. Evalueren van de rol van blockchain en gedistribueerde architecturen in datagedreven systemen. Specifiek:

- Beschrijven en modelleren van een high-level architectuur met gedistribueerde elementen (zoals blockchain)

- Verschillen analyseren tussen conventionele en gedistribueerde databases

- De technische implicaties evalueren van een gedistribueerde database-architectuur (voor bv privacy, controle)

3. Analyseren van de rol van AI in een sociotechnische systeem, en de gevolgen daarvan voor architectuur en waardecreatie. Specifiek:

- Positie van AI in een organisatie modelleren, inclusief ethische en normatieve aspecten

- Design trade-offs analyseren (bijv. transparantie, bias, controle) in de toepassing van AI

4. Modelleren van enterprise-architecturen en businessmodellen voor I&C-toepassingen, en analyseren van bijbehorende ontwerpkeuzes. Specifiek:

- De enterprise-architectuur modelleren van een gegeven I&C-toepassing

- Het business model modelleren van een gegeven I&C-toepassing

- Analyseren van uitdagingen en kansen op basis van architectuur en businessmodel, inclusief het vergelijken van alternatieven

5. Integreren van technische, organisatorische en waardeaspecten in een ontwerpvoorstel voor een I&C-toepassing. Specifiek:

- Samenbrengen van inzichten uit EA, businessmodellen en waardeanalyse rond een maatschappelijk probleem

- Onderbouwde keuzes maken en adviseren over de inrichting van een datagedreven architectuur

description:
Many transportation problems are tackled with quantitative methods, due to the necessity for the decision-makers to quantify relevant aspects: service frequencies, sequence of visits, costs, timings, etc. In this course, we will propose three fundamental methodologies in the transport domain to give answers to problems related to passengers mobility and freight transport.

Discrete choice modelling will be proposed to solve passengers mobility related problems. The goal is to understand how individuals choose between different transport options based on a set of features and related utility functions.

Simulation and mixed-integer linear programming models will be studied to model both operational and strategic decisions related to freight transport. The proposed models are extensively used in container transport, parcel delivery, and trucking problems. Commercial optimization and simulation software will be used to solve the models and analyse the solutions.
learning_objectives:
At the end of this course you will be able to:

- Apply basic discrete choice modelling techniques

- Perform statistical analysis to draw the main elements of the choice models

- Model transportation systems by means of conceptual models and simulation

- Recognize and develop the right mathematical model for a given transportation problem;

- Analyse solutions and perform sensitivity analyses with ad-hoc software.

description:
What does it take to be an entrepreneur?

An entrepreneurial mindset is one that is able to manage risk, identify opportunities and finally, innovate, develop and execute ideas that are commercially viable and feasible.

In the course Entrepreneurial Thinking you will explore and apply different theories and practices that contribute to your ability to think and act more entrepreneurially. More specifically, you will learn about and reflect on individual entrepreneurial traits, understand the concept of, and conduct riskiest assumption tests, learn how to evaluate the desirability, feasibility and viability of a proposed idea. Additionally, you will dive into the theories of entrepreneurial learning.

It is your job to translate the theories discussed and practiced in class and make them applicable to your project. How entrepreneurial is your project? And how can you make it more entrepreneurial? As such, it is expected that you apply what you have learnt in this course to the projects of your fieldwork period in the Global South.
learning_objectives:
Learning objective 1: To reflect on the EntreComp entrepreneurial competencies.

Learning objective 2: To identify an entrepreneurial opportunity to create value in the context of your project.

Learning objective 3: To co-create desirable, feasible and viable value propositions for your project that are competitive.

Learning objective 4: To conduct riskiest assumptions tests that rapidly evaluate the riskiest assumptions about the desirability, feasibility and viability of your entrepreneurial project.

Learning objective 5: To estimate the costs and return of investments of your entrepreneurial project and how these numbers can be translated into business models that are financially robust, environmentally conscious and socially impactful.

Learning objective 6: To present your entrepreneurial project in the form of an elevator pitch in order to mobilize others.

course_name: Preparations for Intercultural Research Project Project Research and Design
description:
This course aims to prepare its participants in designing their intercultural research projects as first-time researchers as part of the minor International Entrepreneurship and Development. The course focuses on various research approaches, methods, and techniques for the participants to conduct research projects within the minor International Entrepreneurship and Development.

The course provides a set of lectures, including research methods, project management, conversational interviews, reading assignments, and in-class discussions combined with group assignments. The participants will work with their project team and reflect on various research approaches, methods, and techniques in workshop sessions which are the main activities throughout the course.

The participants will work with their project team and participate in coaching sessions and do assignments that help them prepare for the upcoming internship project in Q2. At the end of this course, the participants will produce a report and a presentation based on the result of the intercultural research project for their upcoming field trip.
learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, together with your team you should be able to:

LO1: Formulate a value-based mission statement for their upcoming intercultural research project. 

LO2: Setup expert consultation meetings to prepare and get feedback on the plans for the upcoming intercultural research project.

LO3: Design a travel safety plan for the upcoming intercultural research project.

LO4: Design a detailed project plan for the upcoming intercultural research project including the steps provided in the “project plan requirements” document.

LO5: Reflect on the team’s strategies and decisions made in the course based on the acquired knowledge during the project preparation.

course_name: Responsible Management of Risk, Safety and Security
description:
Introduction to the field of risk and safety/ security based on various texts (book, scientific papers and book chapters). In the course, safety and security are considered from multiple perspectives (industrial safety, transport safety, organisational safety, societal safety, occupational safety, fire safety, structural safety, physical security, cyber security). Methods and techniques will be taught to model the factors which influence safety and security in these domains (technical-, human-, and organisational factors), by adopting a decomposition approach of the overall socio-technical system.

Methods and techniques of safety-by-design and security-by-design principles for systems and processes are taught to inherently reduce risks of failure during the life cycle of these systems and processes. Examples of fault-tolerant design, fail-safe design, fool/hufter-proof design in the above domains are discussed.
learning_objectives:
In this course, students will be introduced to safety and security risk management as it is applied in multiple domains. The focus is on how responsible decisions on safety and security, using the concepts of risk, can be made, in particular in the design phase of systems and processes.

Students learn to understand and use the concept of risk in safety and security settings, being aware of its benefits and limitations. They acquire practical knowledge and skills that allow them to describe the safety and security in qualitative and quantitative terms, to investigate the factors which have an impact on safety and security, and to derive and analyse decisions on safety- and security measures, made by risk managers.

The course starts with safety risk first (accidents), and then extends its scope to security risks (threats and attacks).

The following topics will be covered:

Introduction of important safety and risk concepts, such as probability, frequency, hazard/ threat, vulnerability, impact/ consequence

Short history of safety and risk thinking

The management of risk and safety in public and private organisations

Similarities and differences between safety and security risks

Quantitative and qualitative assessment of safety and security risks

Several risk analysis techniques such as fault/ attack trees, hazard "barrier" target HBT-model and bowties

The psychology of safety and security, human error

A systems view on safety/ security

The principles of safe-by-design and security-by-design

During the course various reports on risk/ safety topics in media will be discussed.

After this course, students are able to:

Understand, apply, and quantify risk and related concepts in safety and security settings, as well as reasoning about these

Explain the similarities and differences between safety and security risks and their assessment

Understand the tasks and responsibilities of the safety/ risk manager or professional

Apply several safety and security risk analysis techniques such as fault and attack trees

Make well-founded decisions regarding safety or security issues and countermeasures, explain these choices and communicate them

Apply the safe-by-design and security-by-design principles

description:
Summary

In this course we focus on essential elements when starting a technology-based startup. The aim is to understand the commercial potential of implementing new technology and how to organize a startup to bring the product, process or service into the market. You will learn about technology-based innovations and business model innovations to bring new products and services to the market.

During the course, we touch on various items, considered to be essential for technology-based entrepreneurship such as intellectual property rights, technology development, strategic market and value chain positioning and the role of entrepreneurial ecosystems to support the growth of newly founded startups.

You will learn about the process of opportunity identification and the dynamics of early growth of new firms. Entrepreneurs of starting companies are highly dependent on the information they acquire among potential customers and external stakeholders such as venture capitalists, banks, suppliers and partner firms. We will discuss how entrepreneurs operate in these networks, take benefit from these networks and how they make decisions in such networks. In particular, start-up firms are likely to collaborate with larger incumbent firms which have a very different approach to the management of their business as compared to start-ups. Knowing the difference and how to operate in such instances makes the entrepreneur more resilient and successful. Finally, you will learn about the internal organization of the firm and team development during stages of growth.

Important element of the course is critical thinking. Entrepreneurship is very diverse, manifests in various forms and situations. The variety of entrepreneurship is impossible to capture in a single model, concept or tool. These models, concepts and tools have great benefits for certain forms and situations of entrepreneurship but lack usefulness in other. To be successful as an entrepreneur, it is key to understand when models, concepts and tools make sense.

The Case Analysis of a Technological Enterprise (TBM017A) forms the integration moment of the Minor Technology-Based Entrepreneurship (MOT-MI-088-19), in which the learned knowledge and skills from the individual minor courses (modules) come together. Nothing is as instructive as getting to work yourself to apply all the knowledge learned. The goal is to develop an (own) innovative idea into a realistic market proposition. Each team, consisting of 5 students from different disciplines, comes up with an innovative product idea and develops it on the basis of assignments and examples. The guiding principle for this course is the Disciplined Entrepreneurship method of Bill Aulet. This textbook is mandatory and will be used cover-to-cover. The book is accessible online via TU Delft library account. However, it is advisable to buy the paper version of this book so that you can quickly browse it and paste Post-It's and take notes in relevant places. It is a useful purchase because you will often fall back on it.

The integration course ends with the delivery and presentation of a business plan in which the idea is described, but especially the way in which it meets a need and how you will meet it.

Following individual courses in this minor is not allowed, the teacher of the course can make an exception in different cases.

This course introduces students to the fundamentals of marketing for early-stage ventures, with a specific focus on technology and healthcare-driven innovations. Students will explore how start-ups, particularly in fields such as medical technology, can understand customer needs, design value propositions, position themselves in the market, and develop effective go-to-market strategies.

The course takes a learner-led and practice-oriented approach. Students will work on real-world cases in groups, supported by lectures, case discussions, and in-class exercises. Emphasis is placed on the intersection of marketing, innovation, and systemic thinking, with examples from digital health and medical devices.

Topics covered:

Rather than teaching marketing as a static discipline, this course explores how it functions as a dynamic capability in start-ups. Topics include:

Identifying customer problems and unmet needs: Understand how to define and segment markets, especially in entrepreneurial and innovation-driven contexts.

Crafting compelling value propositions: Learn how to align your offering with the needs of users, buyers, and other stakeholders, particularly in healthcare settings.

Strategic positioning and competitive differentiation: Explore how start-ups can differentiate themselves in crowded markets through clear strategy and effective communication.

Designing customer journeys and go-to-market plans: Analyze routes to market, stakeholder engagement, and how to build trust in innovation ecosystems.

Marketing in transition - from products to services and ecosystems: Reflect on digital transformation, sustainability, and platform-based models as they reshape start-up strategy, especially in the medtech space.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, students will be able to:

Identify target markets and user needs relevant to early-stage ventures

Develop and evaluate value propositions that resonate with both users and institutional buyers

Formulate go-to-market strategies that account for complexity and uncertainty

Apply core marketing concepts to the context of healthcare and medical innovation

Reflect on future trends and strategic directions for marketing in start-ups

course_name: Managing Start-ups: Teamwork, Leadership and AI
description: When technological start-ups launch a product, process, or service in the market, they have to deal with various management issues, such as issues concerning organizational structure, leadership, and Artificial Intelligence (AI). During this course, students learn about the specific risks and opportunities startups face in management compared to more traditional organisations. Students also learn about AI in recruitment and AI HRM tools for startups, as well as their strengths and weaknesses. Finally, students will be introduced to new regulations of AI and online platforms.
learning_objectives:
1. Students can distinguish and recognize different types of organizational structures. They can describe the risks and opportunities of startups compared to other (types of) organisations.

2. Students can describe the group processes that can occur in startups and what the risks and opportunities of these processes are for staff performance. They can formulate strategies to reduce these risks and exploit the opportunities.

3. Students are able to identify leadership styles and to name the advantages and disadvantages of these styles.

4. Students are able to classify and identify the different types of power most important for human resource management.

5. Students are able to identify AI tools used for recruitment and HRM of startups and identify the strengths and weaknesses of these tools.

6. Students are able to identify relevant regulations for startups in the domain of online platforms and artificial intelligence.

description:
The aim of the Introduction to MedTech Entrepreneurship is to inspire and prepare students to use their engineering skills and envision novel technologies in order to solve the challenges that patients and health professionals face.

This is a blended course, students are expected to prepare the course material online before coming to class. Workshops and discussions are scheduled in the first two weeks of the MedTech Minor program.

There may be guest lectures, participation to the assigned guest lectures is compulsory. Students are expected to take notes and ask questions during the lectures.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, students are able to:

Present and discuss key challenges for multiple stakeholders in the field of healthcare entrepreneurship for fundamental health sciences and for health service delivery

description:
If you are a student with a technical background, you will often contribute to innovation as a manager, engineer, or researcher in established companies.

Innovation drives economic and social progress. But we also know that innovation can have downsides. Though particular innovation may benefit the company, they may have tremendous social and environmental costs for others.

This course will teach you about the ethics of innovation in established companies. We aim to enable you to understand innovation as a deeply ethical progress with significance far beyond the individual company. And we will look at concrete innovation projects to understand how different criteria for innovation, e.g. from finance, marketing, or strategy, are related and sometimes in tensions and how you can analyse and evaluate them from an ethical perspective.

We will start with a broad question about the social role and responsibility of corporations in society. Some have argued that the only legitimate aim of corporate innovation must be to benefit the shareholders of a corporation. This view is in stark tension with the fact that corporations and their innovations have tremendous and often negative effects on the environment and people outside the circle of shareholders. We will discuss different concepts and ethical theories to analyse and evaluate the responsibility of companies. The ambition of the course is to confront ideal theory with the particularities of practice. Therefore, we will devote some time to think about how the prescriptions of normative theory can be implemented in the real world. This will lead us to discuss the Design for Values approach, an influential approach to implementing responsible innovation that features prominently in the work of TU Delft researchers. In addressing a corporation's role in society, the course will challenge you to think about the fundamental aim of innovation in corporations and introduce them to some fundamental theories from moral philosophy, business ethics, and political economy.

We will then turn to questions about concrete innovation projects. As a future engineer, technology manager, consultant, or researcher who faces concrete innovation projects, you will need to know how companies can live up to their responsibility in practice. It is one thing to know about the responsibilities of corporations in theory, and quite another to translate them to concrete criteria for an innovation in practice. In innovation processes, values often conflict. For example, it may be cost effective to use cheaper materials for a product, which creates a tension from a safety and risk perspective. We will see that tensions between different requirements in an innovation process will often occur. We will discuss how to identify, analyse, and evaluate tensions using concepts and theories from philosophy and you will apply your knowledge to concrete cases, in individual assignments and in groups. Though we will not present an algorithm or ultimate answer for resolving conflicts, we aim to equip you you with the tools and the required critical understanding to innovate responsibly.

As part of the minor Companies and Value Sensitive Innovation, this course will equip you with a more nuanced understanding of the ethical aspects of innovation in general, and with the tools and concepts to better understand how we can innovate in a way that is economically successful while being ethically sensible.
learning_objectives:
LO1. Recognise, explain, and contrast core business ethical theories about the responsibility of corporations in society.

LO2. Analyse and contrast a particular business ethical theory about the responsibility of corporations in society.

LO3. Explain and evaluate different practical approaches for ensuring economically viable and ethically sound innovation, including the Design for Values approach and governance approaches.

LO4. Describe different theoretical and empirical methods for identifying, analysing, and evaluating tensions and between different criteria for evaluating innovations.

LO5. Identify, explain, and evaluate value conflicts between criteria for evaluating innovations using ethical concepts and approaches, including the Design for Values approach.

LO6. Identify the responsibilities of a company in a concrete case in a group based on theoretical considerations and defend an ethical mission for that company.

LO7. Formulate ethical innovation criteria based on a a company's ethical mission, and apply them to analyse and evaluate other innovation criteria in a concrete case.

LO8. Propose a suitable ethics governance to embed ethical guardrails in a concrete innovation case.

description:
The course sets the scene for the minor ‘Business Innovation for Engineers’. It discusses the challenges that companies face in introducing innovations and managing technological development, under the lens of the digital transformation of their key organizational functions. Firms may use innovation to improve their processes or to differentiate their products and services and outperform their competitors. However, the management of innovation is inherently difficult and risky: most new technologies fail to be translated into products and services, and most new products and services are not commercially successes. In short, innovation can enhance competitiveness, but it requires a specific knowledge and management style.

The course adopts an integrative perspective in analysing the innovation management process and discusses how the organizations can search for innovative opportunities, select innovative projects, develop new products/services and capture a social, economic or business value from this process. It also discusses different types of innovation and defines critical elements for building an innovative organization and developing an innovation strategy. In sum, the course presents the main concepts and methods in innovation management and supports them with series of examples and applications from practice.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, students should be able to:

Identify different types and aspects of innovation.

Explain how the organizations can build capabilities for innovation.

Discuss how the organizations search for innovations.

Explain how the organizations select innovation projects, among a range of innovative ideas.

Analyse how the organizations develop a new product, and what strategies they implement in order to meet the stakeholders needs and expectations.

Evaluate the innovation management process, taking into consideration the business, social and economic values of innovation.

description:
Energy systems embrace multiple technologies, sectors, and perspectives. In this course, you will understand the multiscale (i.e. different levels of aggregation, i.e. equipment, household/industry, energy chain, sector, region, country, international, world) and multiperspective (i.e. technical, environmental, economic, social, and governance) nature of the analysis of energy systems. You will be able to (i) apply methodologies to estimate technical, environmental and economic performance and (ii) recommend options to improve performance at different levels of aggregation.

The course provides the foundation for understanding the main elements that characterise energy systems. Special attention is given to global developments and past, current, and future trends. This includes transitioning from a fossil fuel-based system to a climate-neutral energy system and related potentials and scenarios. Energy systems analysis is a field where good argumentation skills are essential, so in addition to calculations, there is a significant focus on critical thinking, discussion, and reflection.
learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, you should be able to:

Discuss the characteristics of an energy system at different levels of aggregation.

Calculate technical, environmental, and economic indicators at different levels of aggregation.

Estimate system performance based on calculated indicators and contextual information.

Compare energy policies and market issues that would impact a selected system at a specific level of aggregation.

description:
Our current society is intrinsically linked with and dependent on technology. Safety and security risks are often associated with these technologies, such as earthquakes associated with gas extraction, the risks of nuclear waste, hacking of self-driving cars, or cybercrime on the internet. This causes society to be constantly exposed to 'risk'. Often, the risk level only becomes known after the technologies have been deployed and undesired events occur. Contrary to relatively well-understood risks in organisations, the introduction of new technologies in society may imply uncertain, unforeseen, and ambiguous (safety and security) risks, and may give rise to societal and political debate.

In this course, you will learn to identify possible (safety and security) risks associated with new technologies, and provide suggestions for responsible design and deployment. In addition, you will learn to investigate the side-effects of technologies, and their potential effect on moral values, such as surveillance technologies and their effects on privacy and inclusion.
learning_objectives:
After this course, you will be able to:

Explain the goals and methods of technology evaluation and assessment, and apply them to a specific case

Identify and analyse possible security and/or safety implications of a (new) technology

Analyse how (new) technologies can be used to improve security and/or safety, and identify and analyse possible side-effects, such as the effect on other values

Provide suggestions for responsible design and deployment of a new technology with respect to security, safety, and other values

Write a technology evaluation and assessment report in a multidisciplinary group

description:
Many entrepreneurship programs are derived from management programs and are intended to teach managers how to become more entrepreneurial, yet they are not aimed at the entrepreneur as such (Katz, 2007). For example, in business schools the focus is much on 'the' ingredient of entrepreneurship: a business plan presented through a series of case studies and lectures (Carrier, 2007, p. 143). While understanding how big organizations and managers think about entrepreneurship is important, in this course we will focus on what it means to be an self-employed entrepreneur, someone who takes the risks on personal account. We will focus on what it takes to become a successful entrepreneur, what entrepreneurial activity is and why teams of entrepreneurs are considered more resilient in the face of uncertainty.

The majority of this course's lectures will take place during the first week of the minor programme, serving as an intensive kick-off. This week will also focus on forming the teams for the core project that you will develop across multiple courses throughout the minor.
learning_objectives:
You will further develop your competence for self-directed and entrepreneurial learning. You'll learn to see and initiate new opportunities in an imaginative way within the Minor TBE.

You provide evidence of the development of your entrepreneurial competences by means of an (orally) delivered coherent and gripping story that is supported by annotated documentation of your learning attempts.

You can give useful and to-the-point feedback on the team members or other fellow students.

You can reformulate/reframe the feedback you have received either by lecturers or other fellow students into meaningful new learning objectives for the Minor and the semester thereafter.

You become a highly functional part of your team by i.e. recognizing your own role within that team and proposing well-founded interventions to improve your work and team dynamics.

course_name: Researching Cascading Effects: Understanding the Ripple Effects of Cybersecurity Events
description:
In today's interconnected digital landscape, the impact of cybersecurity events extends far beyond their initial occurrence. The course "Researching Cascading Effects: Understanding the Ripple Effects of Cybersecurity Events" is designed to build on knowledge gained during minor and major studies by analyzing cyber incidents and forecasting the consequences stemming from them.

Throughout this course, students will explore cybersecurity events and predict their cascading effects on individuals, organizations, and society as a whole. By examining real-world cases, they will gain a comprehensive understanding of the multifaceted nature of cybersecurity incidents and how exploited vulnerabilities can trigger chain reactions of disruption across various sectors.

As part of the coursework, students will collaborate on a group report analyzing the root causes of a cybersecurity incident. Additionally, each student will produce an individual report assessing its potential cascading effects within the area of their major studies.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, the student should be able to:

Analyze real cybersecurity incidents and identify their causes

Forecast potential cascading effects of real cybersecurity incidents on individuals, organizations, societies and ecosystems

Estimate the impact and probabilities of such events

Work and communicate effectively with students with other disciplinary backgrounds

Apply knowledge by producing a group and an individual reports with the results of the analyses in a specified format

description:
This course introduces the fundamental principles of marketing in the context of technological innovation and engineering-oriented environments. It focuses on how organizations can bring new technologies to market by identifying opportunities, understanding user needs, crafting compelling value propositions, and building effective commercialization strategies.

The course emphasizes strategic thinking and practical application, with a focus on the role of marketing within the broader innovation process. Through team-based work and interactive class sessions, students will apply key frameworks and tools to analyze marketing challenges and develop structured approaches to market entry and growth.

Topics covered:

The course is organized around the following core themes:

Foundations of B2B Marketing and Value Creation
Introduction to marketing principles, the evolution of marketing practices, and the strategic role of marketing in technology-based firms.

Market Segmentation and Customer Value Propositions
Identifying, segmenting, and prioritizing customer groups based on their needs, behaviors, and strategic relevance, and designing value propositions that address those needs.

Strategic Marketing Planning and Positioning
Using marketing tools and frameworks to evaluate market opportunities, define competitive positioning, and guide long-term growth strategies.

Customer Journeys, Sales Approaches, and Communication
Understanding customer decision-making, designing effective go-to-market strategies, and building strong customer relationships.

Emerging Trends and the Future of Innovation Marketing
Exploring how digitalization, service orientation, and ecosystem-based strategies are reshaping modern B2B marketing.
learning_objectives:
After completing this course, students will be able to:

Understand fundamental B2B marketing concepts and how they contribute to competitive advantage in innovation-oriented firms

Apply strategic tools to analyze marketing challenges and identify growth opportunities in technological and business environments

Segment markets, identify target customers, and develop appropriate value propositions based on business needs

Understand customer journeys and apply this knowledge to craft effective marketing strategies

Design strategic marketing plans aimed at long-term business development and customer retention

Evaluate marketing performance using appropriate criteria and consider the impact of emerging technologies and business models

Analyze trends in B2B marketing, including digital transformation, AI, international marketing, and ecosystem collaboration

Communicate insights clearly and collaborate effectively in teams to solve marketing challenges

description:
The core objective of this course is to enhance decolonial and regenerative-oriented critical thinking on their project in communities in Africa, Latin America, and Southeast Asia contexts from decolonial, pluriverse, and regenerative perspectives that will contribute to your project design process to be as much as co-participatory, balancing power dynamics on decision-making processes and value and recognize local knowledge systems as a pathway for social justice. This course is about decolonial participatory design, alternative forms of entrepreneurship for collective action, social justice, and the dynamics of domination and resistance at personal, community, and institutional levels that the historically underrepresented communities that you will work alongside in Africa, Latin America, Southeast Asia, have been enduring In essence, it is a call for us to heed the growing critiques of the ways that design, innovation, and entrepreneurship (of images, objects, software, algorithms, sociotechnical systems, the built environment, indeed, everything we make) too often contributes to the reproduction of systemic oppression. To advance the growing conversation about the pitfalls and possibilities of design and entrepreneurship as a tool for social transformation, the course gravitated around the concept, principles, and perspectives of decolonization, regeneration, and pluriverse.

“The pluriverse is an acknowledgment that we do not live in a single world with different belief systems, paradigms, or cultures; instead, the pluriverse suggests that we live in a world of many worlds. This phrasing, ‘a world of many worlds’, is essential in its formulation: on the one hand, there is one world – we share a material existence, we are connected in and through relations of power, and we also often share concepts, language, practices, and other aspects of our collective forms of life. At the same time, however, there are many worlds; there are different collective worlding practices that enact different worlds, and these worlds are sometimes in excess of each other.”  (Meggie FitzGerald, 2022).  The feasibility of your project will be in terms of your ability to recognize and navigate the local knowledge systems of your project´s context, aiming to create community-led interventions that envision alternative futures and support just regenerative communities. You will immerse in methods such as privilege, access power, racialized-minority entrepreneurship, Indigenous knowledge systems, inclusive language, decolonizing engineering and design for regeneration, storytelling and other ethnographic methods, circular communities, and developing alternative future scenarios for community-based interventions.

The students will work in groups and individually in different assessment formats that will actively enhance critical thinking in oral discussions in class, story mapping, ethnographic methods (storytelling interview techniques, active observation, observation plan, tec), and individual reflections (Journaling).
learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, you should be able to:

LO1: Evaluate foundational preconditions for creating regenerative projects by incorporating pluriverse perspectives, decolonial theories, inclusive language, and decolonial participatory design practices.

LO2: Critically examine the limitations and assumptions underlying mainstream sustainable development narratives, emphasizing how historical context, power access dynamics, privilege, and coloniality perpetuate systemic oppression within design and engineering practices in your projects in Africa, Latin America, and Southeast Asia.

LO3: Articulate and critically analyze how your project explicitly integrates pluriverse perspectives, regeneration, inclusive and empowering language, decolonial theories, and participatory design methods, challenging traditional design/engineering approaches and enhancing community-led projects.

LO4: Assess the multiple dimensions of value creation in your project, considering regenerative principles, circularity, community well-being, and alternative economic systems informed by pluriverse and decolonial frameworks.

LO5: Conduct a systematic analysis of external and internal factors—including socio-political trends, local developments, stakeholder dynamics, and uncertainties—that influence your community-led projects, ensuring sustainable and just outcomes within LMIC contexts.

LO6: Facilitate inclusive stakeholder engagement in your project co-design and co-implementation by deliberately applying decolonial principles, recognizing and addressing power imbalances, privilege awareness, and fostering meaningful participatory practices.

description:
The 15 ECTS Q2 module has been designed to allow students to practise and reflect on the theories, skills and tools learned during the first half of the minor. Assuming no safety restrictions, students will travel to complete a practical 2-3-month project hosted by an NGO, startup, (social) enterprise, university or governmental organisation, usually in the Global South.

The academic focus during the module is on applying entrepreneurial and project management skills within a challenge-based and experiential learning pedagogy. In doing so, students will work closely with project stakeholders to understand and consider the local context to develop technical solutions that contribute to sustainable socio-economic development.

Each project has a (local) challenge owner and is co-supervised and graded by a member of TU Delft staff. Some projects may also be coached under supervision by a relevant master's student, e.g. by a recent IED alum, or by an external technical supervisor. Students will work in multi-disciplinary teams to solve their assigned challenges.
learning_objectives:
After completing the intercultural integration project, students will be able:

To develop and execute a solution to a complex socio-technical challenge as presented by their project provider.

To incorporate entrepreneurial competencies and project planning techniques

To manage communication with local stakeholders and the transfer of technology in a culturally sensitive manner.

To improve and reflect on one's own entrepreneurial competencies and role within a startup team

To assess the effectiveness of the project outcomes through a final project group report and storytelling assignment, and present and answer questions about these, either at an interactive project market or to a panel of experts or peers.

description:
Identifying and investing in innovation opportunities is key. In fact, organizations that do not invest in innovation struggle to keep pace with the rapidly changing business environment. However, even the best and most innovative ideas will go nowhere unless we can convince others to commit the necessary resources. That is why finance can play a critical role in helping organizations and investors recognize the value of innovation.

The Financing Innovation course will equip you with the necessary toolkit for using financial statements, performing financial statement analysis, estimating business value, and making financing decisions from the perspective of an innovative company. Understanding the key techniques of financial valuation and capital budgeting used by organizations is essential for project owners (project managers or entrepreneurs) to ensure their ideas get the attention and funding they deserve. More specifically, you will gain experience building a financial model to assess a new product launch. We will consider key financial metrics that are commonly applied and learn which ones are reliable—and which are not. We will also explore how we can use the financial model to guide our efforts as project managers in order to maximize impact. Along the way, we will gain insight into how financial markets work and how investors evaluate stocks and bonds. Finally, we will learn how to use these skills to understand the drivers of a company's value.

The Financing Innovation course complements other fields such as strategy, marketing, and innovation management. In these fields, business decisions—such as which markets or products to invest in—are often formulated. In Financing Innovation, we evaluate these choices and analyze how best to fund them.

The course is relevant for student entrepreneurs, those aspiring to become entrepreneurs, and students aiming to pursue careers in the high-tech sector, consulting, or public institutions that support innovation and entrepreneurship.
learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, you should be able to:

LO1: Discuss the characteristics of at least four types of financing available at different stages of the innovation process (e.g., accelerators, crowdfunding, business angels, and venture capital).

LO2: Interpret the information contained in financial statements (balance sheet, income statement and statement of cash flows) to evaluate firm performance and estimate firm value.

LO3: Apply at least three investment appraisal techniques (e.g., NPV, IRR, Payback Period).

LO4: Estimate the value of financial assets, such as stocks and bonds.

LO5: Apply two different methods to value innovative businesses (e.g., discounted cash flow valuation and valuation by comparables).

description:
The aim of the minor Companies and Value-Sensitive Innovation is to teach students a comprehensive and practical understanding of the innovation process and its ethical dimensions. Management of risk and safety is one of the crucial aspects in order to create ethically sound and economically viable innovations. In this course, you will learn risk management concepts, and you will learn to think in terms of safety- and security-related incident scenarios: what are the causes of unwanted events with regard to safety and security of innovations? And what are possible unwanted consequences? Prevention of these unwanted events, as well as recovery and mitigation if an unwanted event does occur, takes up a central role in the course.

In the course we will look into safety and security risks at different phases of an innovation, being the development phase, the production phase, and the deployment phase (when the innovation is introduced into society). You will learn to identify these risks, analyse them, and formulate recommendations to manage safety and security risks throughout all phases of the innovation process.

When looking into risks emerging from technologies, the observable risks are important to take into account, as well as the perceived risks (opinions and perceptions of different stakeholders). You will learn to analyse the possible societal impact of safety and security risks emerging from innovations, as well as the relations and tensions between safety and security risks and other values such as privacy, transparency, and inclusion.

In the course, we will look into the roles and responsibilities of relevant stakeholders - such as designers and users of innovations - regarding managing safety and security risks.
learning_objectives:
After this course, you will be able to:

1. Identify and analyse safety and security risks associated with innovations throughout the entire innovation process (development, production, deployment)

2. Understand and analyse safety and security scenarios associated with innovations in terms of prevention, recovery, and mitigation, and in terms of observable risks and perceived risks

3. Understand and analyse the potential societal impact of safety and security risks emerging from innovations

4. Understand and evaluate the relations and tensions between safety and security risks and other values such as privacy, transparency, inclusion

5. Formulate recommendations to manage safety and security risks throughout all phases of the innovation process (development, production, deployment)

6. Understand and analyse the roles and responsibilities of managing safety and security risks

description:
The Interdisciplinary Project is the capstone course of the Business Innovation for Engineers minor, designed to integrate knowledge from Finance, Innovation Management, Marketing, Ethics, and Risk and Safety into a real-world business challenge. In this course, students will work in teams to develop a comprehensive Innovation Plan for a real existing company that is actively pursuing a technological breakthrough.
