description:
Intellectual Property (IP) Rights are increasingly important in todays fast-moving, hyper-connected world. Awareness of the different types of IP is of vital importance, not only for lage companies and startups, but also for university researchers and even individuals. Knowing what Intellectual Property is, who owns it, how to protect it, how to trade it, and how to enforce an IP Rights is essential to ensure freedom of operation and keep imitators at bay. In addition to the fundamentals of IP Rights, IP Law and IP Policy are central topics of this course.

Whenever you create something, whether it is an invention, a book, a song, a painting of even a website, chances are that you will have to deal with Intellectual Property and the Rights that are associated with it. There are two sides of the medal: the IP Rights that you own and may have to enforce, and the IP Rights that are not yours and that you will have to deal with.

This course is intended for entrepreneurial engineers in every discipline, whether it be the hard sciences (quantum computing or nanobiology) or the more creative sciences (architecture of industrial design), especially when it concerns innovative products, processes, services and design. Given the increasing demands placed by society on companies and universities to innovate and improve life and society at large, IP rights have become synonymous with successful innovation and startups. Intellectual property rights also play a key role in todays scientific community. Understanding how the legal framework affects both the science and the companies in the business of creating high-tech and innovative solutions for todays problems, is of paramount importance.

In this course you will become familiar with the basics of European IP law and the most common types of IP law (including the requirements to obtain these rights). You will explore the process by which patents are granted, how patent rights can be exercised in court and how they can be used as a business tool. Modern-day IPR issues such as the patentability of computer-implemented inventions and biotech inventions will be addressed. Additionally, software protection (including open source) works and the related issues will be discussed. The topics will be presented on the basis of real-life cases. During the course, participants will analyze and present a case in which a university spin-off is confronted with a multitude of IP issues.
learning_objectives:
Get to know the basics of European IP Law

Understand the common types of IP law

Understand the requirements to obtain IPR

Understand the process of granting patents

Understand how to exercise patent rights in court

Understand how to use patent rights as a business modeling tool

Understand patent rights in different industries

description:
New technologies, such as hydrogene, AI, robotics, data analytics, etc, provide great potential for large firms and public organizations. The speed by which these technologies develop and the expertise that is needed pose a challenge for these organizations to follow and exploit the potential. Although the have more financial capital, better access to markets, and more technological knowledge, we often see that large firms and public organizations work with startups to investigate the potential of the new technologies for their business.

In this course, we focus on the strategies that large firms and public organizations use to engage startups, experiment with new technologies and co-create together to develop new business opportunities. We will investigate the organizational settings for collaboration and we will pay specific attention to the emergence of academic start-ups and how large firms and public organizations provide incubation facilities and financial support (venture capital) to engage with these startups to renew themselves.

This course examines the various forms of corporate entrepreneurship and the relationship with their technology strategy in particular. You will develop knowledge and skills to analyze strategic situations and design the most appropriate solutions in terms of corporate entrepreneurship strategy and startup engagement.

Summary

This course examines how large firms and public organizations engage with startups to tap into new technologies to open new markets based on renewed business models.

You will develop knowledge and skills to analyse strategic situations of existing organizations and how they innovate by engaging startups. The course provides an eye on corporate startup engagement from both the large organization and startup perspective.
learning_objectives:
Understand the concept of corporate entrepreneurship; the contexts, the forms, and the relationship with strategic management

Analyze strategic situations and design appropriate corporate entrepreneurship strategies and organizations

Analyse the contribution of internal and external ventures in the renewal of large corporates

Understand the emergence of academic spin-offs and how they relate to the technology development of large established organisations

Identify the various key actors that facilitate and support the emergence of new business ventures and academis spin-offs

description:
The course "Business Strategies for Digital Transformation" focuses on the strategic decisions and capabilities that organizations need to develop in response to digitalization, service innovation, and sustainability transitions. It examines how companies can adjust their strategies, business models, and operations to remain competitive in rapidly evolving environments.

Students will learn how to develop strategic approaches that support innovation, long-term growth, and responsible value creation. The course emphasizes real-world application through group work, case discussions, and interactive lectures. By the end of the course, students will have a deeper understanding of how to navigate and lead strategic transformation in technology-driven industries.

Topics covered:

The course is organized around the following interlinked themes:

Rethinking Strategy in the Digital Age
Shifts in strategy logic, value creation in digital contexts, and the transformation imperative.

Business Model Innovation and Strategic Adaptation
Redesigning how firms create, deliver, and capture value in dynamic environments.

From Products to Services and Solutions
Transitioning toward service-based business models and understanding servitization strategies.

Ecosystem Thinking and Platform Strategies
Competing and collaborating through ecosystems, partnerships, and platform models.

Data, Digital Technologies, and Strategic Capabilities
Leveraging digital tools and organizational capabilities for transformation.

Sustainable and Responsible Strategy Design
Aligning growth with long-term societal and environmental impact.

Synthesis and Strategic Foresight
Integrating insights, planning under uncertainty, and preparing for the future.
learning_objectives:
After completing this course, students will be able to:

Analyze how digitalization, servitization, and sustainability reshape business strategy

Redesign and innovate business models and value propositions for changing environments

Evaluate how ecosystems and platform dynamics influence strategic decision-making

Apply service-oriented logic to develop long-term customer and stakeholder value

Assess internal capabilities required for strategic transformation and agility

Develop strategies that integrate technological innovation with responsible growth

Use foresight techniques to plan for uncertain and rapidly evolving futures

description:
This course focuses on financing of technology ventures and innovation from three different points of view  that of an entrepreneur, a professional investor, and a policy-maker.

From the entrepreneurs point of view, we will discuss financing strategies for different business models at the different stages of startup formation and examine the entrepreneurial finance industry: the sources of startup funding (from crowdfunding and venture capital to governments and corporations), motivations of entrepreneurs and investors, and the contracts between them (e.g. convertible note, equity deals, etc.). We also explore latest developments in entrepreneurial finance in more depth (e.g. crowdfunding, venture studios). Also, we'll explore the basics of corporate governance important for startups (i.e. ownership, vesting schedule, control, and legal structure).

From the professional investors angle, we will be discussing tools and concepts as well as evidence and metrics that are essential when assessing startups viability and profitability at different stages. We will go in more depth with techniques used to evaluate startups (i.e. discounted cash flow, real options, comparables, etc.).

Lastly, we view the startup financing from the point of view of public and social impact investors and policy-makers that want to spur entrepreneurship and innovation through financing deep technology startups, and discuss major challenges in financing ventures with long and uncertain R&D, and the macroenvironments effect on startup financing.

The class lies at the intersection of academic research and insights from practice. The course is especially suitable for master students that are interested in (or in the process of) starting or joining a technology startup, as well as for those who are curious about the process and challenges of technology venture and innovation financing. The course is highly recommended for students who are considering developing a master thesis in this area.

Throughout the course, participants will learn to distinguish between emerging and disruptive technologies, understand influential dynamics such as innovation diffusion, hypes and emotions, and develop the methodical competencies to assess and evaluate an emerging technology in an environment of high information asymmetry. The goal is to learn to leverage the potential of emerging and digital innovations within a specific industry.

Summary

This course offers the fundaments of digital entrepreneurship and the management of emerging (digital) technologies. In this course, participants choose an upcoming digital technology of interest and assess it with different methods from multiple angles to evaluate its ability to create a competitive advantage or disrupt an industry or market. This course helps participants prepare for various career paths, from launching their product/service as an entrepreneur to making informed technology adoption and rejection decisions as an intrapreneur.
learning_objectives:
Upon finishing the course, participants will be able to:

LO 1 Describe the difference between emerging and disruptive technologies.

LO 2 Understand current social and market dynamics that influence the diffusion and success of emerging technologies.

LO 3 Develop a critical perspective on conflicting stakeholder interests.

LO 4 Analyse an emerging technology's potential for a specific market/industry/company.

LO 5 Adapt a business plan to the realities of digital technology.

LO 6 Make informed decisions in the context of high information asymmetries.

course_name: Idea to Start-up – IT and AI
description:
You will focus on information and computing technologies (e.g AI, big data, blockchain) that are transforming traditional industries and societies at large.

To analyse the opportunities for new startups we focus on entrepreneurial tools such as the opportunity canvas; value proposition development and customer empathy mapping, market segmentation and value chain analyses and the initial operations to develop a minimum viable product.

Summary

In this course, you do not study entrepreneurship, you become an entrepreneur. Working in a team, you identify a business opportunity using emerging digital technologies. Applications can range from mobility, cyber security to predictive maintenance etc. You will test its validity, and build a viable business model, a roadmap from an idea to an innovation-driven company. On this journey, you will be coached by lecturers and learn practical insights from guest lecturers from industry and the startup ecosystem. After this course, you will be able to proactively assess the merit of a technology startup, whether you want to build one or join one.
learning_objectives:
Develop a business Idea by identifying a relevant economic problem or unmet need that is addressed by digital solutions, and advanced information and computing technologies.

Conduct primary and secondary market research in order to rigorously test the value of your business idea and to identify an appropriate market segment

Analyse the competitive landscape and devise your products competitive advantage, given specific challenges of protecting IP in the digital world. Create a blueprint of your product.

Identify relevant stakeholders in your startups ecosystem, outline the go-to-market strategy, and assess profitability. Understand how these strategies adjust when trying to implement your solution in well-established systems of traditional industries.

Integrate and convincingly present all the aspects of your business idea into a coherent business model supported by collected evidence.

Emulate effective entrepreneurial behaviour by rapidly gathering new information and acting on it by improving the business model.

Evaluate your entrepreneurial skills and motivate constructive feedback through peer reviewing

course_name: Idea to Start-up - Health and Life Sciences
description:
We will make use of various methods, tools and techniques to develop a sound business plan:

- Opportunity canvas

- Value proposition development and customer empathy

- Market segmentation

- Value chain analyses

- Stakeholder mapping

- Competitive advantage analysis

- Minimum viable product development

- Key resource and capability analysis

Summary

In this course, you do not study entrepreneurship, you become an entrepreneur. Working in a team, you identify a business opportunity, validate it, and build a viable business model, a roadmap from an idea to a sustainable innovation-driven company. After this course, you will be able to proactively assess the merit of a technology startup, whether you want to build one or join one.

During the eight teaching sessions we investigate societal challenges, how technology can address these and the way in which we can create viable entrepreneurial business opportunities. As a framework for this, we use the business planning process and students develop the essential parts of a business plan and investor pitch as to achieve this goal.

Students will work in teams to develop a minimum viable business proposition. Central are the methodologies to conduct opportunity identification, market analysis, technology viability assessment, competitive positioning, team-building, product life-cycle planning, marketing strategy, sales channel analysis.

Personal development is important and in the course of the program students will learn to think as an entrepreneur and act as a salesperson; a champion that has a specific eye for longevity of the business, sustaining growth and responsible innovation.

Enrollment is through Brightspace (Osiris is not needed).
learning_objectives:
After completing this course you have a firm understanding of

1.Define the potential market segments and develop market research and segmentation for start-ups, through interaction with potential clients.

2.Develop a stakeholder map and recognise potential supporters and opponents and turn them into your favour (Include Health organizations, Insurance companies and other important players in the health care)

3.Reflect on leading a medical product design process how to manage actors and stakeholders to achieve their business goals

4.Identify the potential characteristics of your end user by developing persona through empathy map.

5.Ethics of collaboration with Doctors and Patients.

6.Design a medical product launch strategy and define steps for action for a specific National Systems

7.Define several potential launch strategies country depending on the needs of your product. (FDA, Insurance,)

8.Identify and develop your ideas into start-ups and analyze different factors to identify opportunities based on opportunity analysis canvas.

9.Identify and describe the main challenges or critical junctures that your company might face in the initial growth stages and describe the main activities that your company should follow to mitigate them.

10.Describe and apply the generic pattern of development and diffusions for your radically new high-tech products and identify the position of your innovative product in the pattern.

11.Identify your beach head market and calculate the TAM, SAM, SOM size for beachhead market.

12.Develop a stakeholder map and recognise potential supporters and opponents and turn them into your favour.

13.Conduct a competitor analysis and identify the main competitors that offer the alternatives and compare and analysis these alternatives against your proposition.

14.Describe the business model canvas that outlines the business case for your new product/service.

15.Calculate the Lifetime value of an Acquired Customer and calculate the Cost of Customer Acquisition

16.Define your initial Minimum Viable Business Product (MVP)

17.Make a first overview of your cash flow projections for the first 2-3 years based on the costs of product development and production, costs of marketing and sales effort and expected income generated

course_name: Idea to Start-up - Energy and Sustainability
description:
The course stimulates and assists students in creating a sustainable business idea and assessing the feasibility and the market potential thereof by testing it against prospective customers and key players in the specific industry of application.

Business ideas must be in the domain of energy or sustainability. A sustainable business idea is a product, a process or a service that enables sustainability, where sustainability is defined as the capacity for the biosphere and human civilization to co-exist indefinitely.

Students work together in teams which will be self-formed or if needed formed by the instructor.

Each team needs to come up with an original sustainable startup idea, or a sustainable business idea connected to pressing sustainability challenges of our day.

Each sustainable business idea must be technology-based: we do not accept apps and definitely no consulting of any kind.

The course consists of two interconnected parts:

1. Students attend lectures and workshops.

2. Teams carry out a feasibility study for their sustainable business idea.
learning_objectives:
- Develop a business idea in the domain of energy & sustainability.

- Test the value and the feasibility of your business idea and analyze the market potential of the product.

- Develop a blueprint of your product and map its position in a competitive landscape.

- Formulate business models and a go-to-market strategy.

- Perform initial assessment of the profitability of the business idea.

- Gain practical knowledge about starting up a business.

- Give a convincing business presentation.

- Emulate effective entrepreneurial behavior.

description:
In this course, you do not study entrepreneurship, you become an entrepreneur. Working in a team, you identify a business opportunity, test its validity, and build a viable business model a roadmap from an idea to a sustainable innovation-driven company. On this journey, you will be helped by guest lecturers from industry and the startup ecosystem. After this course, you will be able to proactively assess the merit of a technology venture, whether you want to build or join one. While the starting point is tackling the societal and market problems and unmet needs, the solution ideas must be based on substantial scientific advances and cutting-edge engineering that can be used to build competitive advantage in the market (via patent for example). Feel free to bring your own ideas and technologies, but you do not need one to enjoy this course. All you need is curiosity about building a business on solid technological foundations.

Fast-paced and interactive, the class consists of mostly coaching sessions and team exercises, therefore class attendance is very important. Online content and short in-class lectures provide you with general guidelines for each business model milestone. There will be weekly assignments, building blocks to a full-fledged business model. Final deliverables include: a logbook of primary market research (yes, you'll do interviews!), business model report, and a pitch presentation in front of a jury of startup professionals.

You start the course with forming teams around a market problem or unmet need. Then, you gradually build a business model, mainly by answering questions such as: Who are my customers and what value do I create for them? How big is this market? How should my minimum viable product look like? How do I build a competitive advantage in the market (e.g. by patenting)? How will I market and deliver this product to the customer? Can this be a profitable business? You seek answers through customer, stakeholder, and expert interviews, by developing step-by-step interview protocols and executing them.
learning_objectives:
- Develop a business idea based on a relevant economic problem or unmet need.

- Conduct primary and secondary market research in order to rigorously test the value of your business idea and to identify an appropriate market segment

- Develop a blueprint of your product and map its position in a competitive landscape.

- Identify relevant stakeholders in your startups ecosystem.

- Formulate a business model and a go-to-market strategy.

- Perform initial assessment of the profitability of the business idea.

- Integrate and convincingly present all the aspects of your business idea into a coherent business model supported by collected evidence.

- Emulate effective entrepreneurial behaviour by rapidly gathering new information and acting on it by modifying the business model.

course_name: Regenerative Entrepreneurship in the Global South
description:
In this course, you will work in a team to identify a start-up or challenge opportunity in regenerative and circular entrepreneurship. You will challenge the as-usual buzzword narrative entrepreneurship that only focuses on the solution-profit drive mission. Instead, you will analyze a global/regional/national/local context and look at the social, economic, environmental, political, cultural, and entrepreneurial ecosystem synergies and trade-offs from a challenge taking place in the “Global South” and co-develop an intervention concept that tackles a challenge given by our challenge owners from South-east Asia, Latin America, and Africa. You will go from testing the intervention idea´s validity to building a viable business model with local partners incorporating their local systems knowledge, ethnographic methods, and decolonial participatory design methods. This course focuses on diving deep into regenerative and circular entrepreneurship and developing regenerative/circular business models that generate positive well-being, and social and environmental impacts that prioritize the voices and needs of the local grassroots organizations.

You will focus on creating innovative interventions for some of today’s urgencies. Transforming the value chain for unique marine biodiversity hotspots, thinking along on bio-inspired solutions, and working in rural agro-forestry farming with local historically underrepresented communities are some topics you will dive deep into during the course. The course narrative is built around entrepreneurial tools and alternative systems knowledge such as regenerative leadership, storytelling, skills for a new wave of change-makers, regenerative value proposition, stakeholder analyses, and regenerative business modelling to analyse opportunities for regenerative and emancipatory entrepreneurial solutions for and with local communities.
learning_objectives:
By the end of this course, you should be able to:

Macro Level: Learning block 1 - Regenerative Shared Value Creation & Introducing the product to the market.

LO1: Understand the concept and principles of regenerative entrepreneurship and challenges arising from the as-usual forms of entrepreneurship.

LO2: Define the shared value creation from an idea towards a startup intervention to boost societal transitions to regenerative systems for climate action.

LO3: Analyze the competitive landscape (entrepreneurial ecosystems), stakeholders, and local communities’ roles.

LO4: Identify your potential market, beachhead market, and the size of the market.

LO5: Rigorously identifies and applies market research techniques and ethnographic methods to test and validate your intervention idea/concept.

Meso-level -Learning block 2 - Ideation & Air-tight Concept

LO6: Deliver ideas, products, and services in response to regenerative challenges.

LO7: Acquire skills and tools that can be used to facilitate a regenerative entrepreneurial process.

Micro-level - Learning block 3 - The regenerative business model

LO8: Explain and apply methods for creating regenerative business models for your challenge.

LO9: Analyze and identify the factors that will lead to the adoption of regenerative technology innovation for the specific customer segment of your challenge.

description:
Turning Technology into Business (TTiB) aims to equip participants with a strong conceptual foundation to actively understand the dynamic process of technology-based entrepreneurship.
Participants learn how business strategies are best formulated and how (through entrepreneurship) technology can create value.

TTiB consists of seven lectures, introducing the theoretical backgrounds of technological, market and business analyses.
A unique aspect of TTiB is that existing technologies (developed and patented by the TU Delft) are used as case subjects.
The patent project is the focal point of the curriculum.
Each group of 4-5 students will be assigned an original patent, and is expected to evaluate the commercial potential of this technology.
This includes choosing promising applications (products) for the technology, and making recommendations for the most suitable business model to commercialize the technology.
The patent project should provide a coherent and structured answer to the central question: which strategy is most likely to generate business from this patent?
In addition to equipping participants with a thorough knowledge of the course subject, the Delft Center for Entrepreneurship (DCE) hopes that this course will be the starting point for a variety of university spin-offs in which the students will participate.
To accommodate this, DCE offers several follow-up courses.
See: https://www.tudelft.nl/tbm/dce/education/master-courses
learning_objectives:
This course aims to equip students with a strong conceptual foundation to an active understanding of two domains:

(1) The dynamic process of technological innovation through concepts such as technology life-cycles, dominant design, disruptive technologies, Schumpeterian competition and the diffusion of innovations

(2) How business strategies are formulated and, through entrepreneurship, technology can create value. This multi-faceted process of technology commercialization process is addressed in terms of assessing technology position, discovering market opportunities, competitive analysis, appropriability and the various modes of entrepreneurship.

description:
RtS focuses predominantly on Business Strategy: gaining market traction, prototyping, growing the team, devising a financial plan and fundraising strategy, protecting IP, and foundational activities (setting up a company, sharing ownership, etc.)

description:
Join us in an interdisciplinary exploration of technology startup's business model and strategy. This pioneering course offers you an opportunity to work with a technology-based startup from the local ecosystem or a corporate venture in an internship-like setting and help them progress.

In a group of about three students from different faculties and study programs, you will work on:

1) a business challenge in the domain of market research and validation.

2) understanding, reflecting, and advising on the business model, risks, and growth strategies of your assigned startup.

You will be coached and taught solid business theoretical foundation and practical lessons. You will apply your learnings directly, solving pressing business challenges and driving innovation.

This hands-on experience allows to you communicate directly with startup's key decision-makers and see the effects of your work making a difference.

This course is a real-world expedition into the startup life, designed to inspire, challenge, and prepare you for a future where you drive change.

We expect you to spend around three days a week with the startup and about one day a week in the classroom setting. Given its 15 ECTS, we expect your full weekly commitment, as in any joint interdisciplinary project.

The applications opens on April 30th and the application deadline will be on June 15th. Here is the link to the application form (that contains the list of startups):

https://forms.office.com/e/tX9hXqNM7u

You can still apply after the deadline, but you will be admitted to the course only in case there are any open spots available.

What to Expect

Internship-like Experience: Step into the fast-paced world of startup or corporate venture, through our internship-like experience. Here, you'll gain invaluable hands-on exposure to real-world business practices, navigating challenges, and seizing opportunities alongside industry professionals.

Lectures: Immerse yourself in lectures that serve as the cornerstone of your theoretical understanding that will help you with your company project. Topics that will be covered: market analysis and research, business models and market strategies, business risks, and team dynamics, among others.

Coaching Sessions: These sessions help you apply your newfound knowledge and skills to your cases and tackle pressing business challenges head-on, devising innovative solutions that drive tangible impact and transformation.

What You'll Experience and Learn

You will leave your comfort zone as you'll have to immerse yourself in markets and communicate to market experts, industry stakeholders, and startup's customers.

You will gain practical, real-world experience that sets you apart in today's competitive job market. Our internship-like experience and consulting project offer unparalleled opportunities for skill development and professional growth.

Interdisciplinary Exploration: Navigate the complex nexus of diverse disciplinary backgrounds in engineering, basic science and architecture and design, entrepreneurship, and management, transcending traditional disciplinary boundaries to craft innovative business models that redefine the status quo.

Practical Application: Move beyond theoretical concepts and immerse yourself in practical, hands-on experiences. You'll apply cutting-edge techniques and theoretical frameworks to real-world scenarios, honing your problem-solving skills and business acumen.

Networking Opportunities: Forge meaningful connections with industry professionals, guest lecturers, and fellow classmates, expanding your professional network and gaining valuable insights into the startup ecosystem.

Personal and Professional Growth: Reflect on your journey, identify your strengths, and chart a course for future success. Whether it's sharpening your communication skills or refining your leadership abilities, this course offers a transformative experience that extends far beyond the classroom.

Emulate effective entrepreneurial behaviour in decision-making under uncertainty.

Reflect on the evolution of entrepreneurial growth and business model adaptation.

course_name: Introduction to Water Governance in Deltas
description:
Water is of vital importance to human being, especially when living in a delta. Climate change is disrupting business as usual. This intensifies existing issues and introduces new challenges, including more frequent flooding or drought, competition for scarce water resources and deterioration of the conditions for nature in water and land systems. Dealing with these challenges means adaptation. Not only by finding new suitable (technical) solutions, but also by adjusting the organization of water management where necessary.

In this course, we will study the delta as a socio-ecological-technical system, in which you will learn how these sub-systems interact and how they are managed. Most importantly, you will learn to understand and value the context-specificity of water governance in deltas of large river systems. The focus of the course is on governance: the structures and processes in which water policies are formulated and executed. These policies may be aimed at achieving a fair distribution of water as a common pool resource, reduction of risks associated with water or dealing with conflicting interests of stakeholders.

The lecture series touches upon flood risk management, water resources management, urban water management and 'water as a condition for nature and land-use'. Special attention will be given to governance for the adaptation to climate change. While we take the Dutch delta as a starting point, international examples are discussed during the lectures/workshops and your individual assignment may be about a delta of your choice.

Next to lectures, there are two excursions and a panel discussion. The excursions take you on a bicycle tour to explore urban water management in the city of Delft and further into Holland by bus to see water management in deltas in practice. The panel discussion concentrates on the challenge of freshwater management, in particular strategies for drinking water production across policy levels (EU, national and local).

The course offers the basic knowledge about water systems, Dutch water management and especially (water) governance that enables you to engage in issues related to water governance and water system modelling. We provide a framework of reference that enables you to analyse the governance of deltas as socio-ecological-technical systems in deltas. In the individual assignment, you will develop recommendations for the management of freshwater management in deltas. You will combine desk research, interviews and other sources of information to evaluate governance performance and deliver your findings in a communication product (podcast, video, poster or policy brief). With that in mind, the course also intends to stimulate development of personal skills such as curiosity, visual appraisal, engagement with stakeholders, conceptualization of cause-effect chains and communicating your findings. To achieve this, your findings and recommendations are to be presented in a video, podcast, scientific poster or (internet) brochure.
learning_objectives:
After completing this course, you will be able to:

Explain and apply important concepts for governance of water in deltas in relation to different water-related problems and contexts.

Question (Dutch) practices in water governance and comment on the factors that have shaped these practices.

Discuss, and illustrate with examples, the main issues, objectives and means for water governance as related to:

urban water management

water resources management,

river/flood risk management,

water as a condition for nature and land-use

governance of climate change adaptation

Reflect on dealing with spatial and temporal scales in governance of water in deltas.

Draw conceptual models that explain the functioning of socio-ecological-technical system, including the cause-effect chains for water-related issues in deltas and the main factors that steer system performance.

Communicate and motivate your recommendation for governance of freshwater management in deltas:

with respect to the historical, present and future performance of the water system;

while making use of visual appraisal, stakeholder interviews and other resources of information.

description: This hands-on modeling course gives an introduction to overarching challenges of water and delta systems and their assessment when facing multiple sources of uncertainty, multiple-competing demands and challenging climate and demographic conditions. Upon completion, the students are expected to have command of different water and delta systems and their modeling challenges for assessment and policy making.

LO2. Students can apply the principles of strategic planning and implement it to a water policy problem that is typical for urbanizing deltas, and communicate the findings.

LO4. Students have knowledge of decision support and data-management tools that are typically used in water management, and have insight into when to (not) use these and how to deal with relevant uncertainties.

description:
The course deals with the following subjects: 1. Introduction to Building with Nature, 2. Engineering design principles, 3. Ecological design principles, 4. Integrated BwN design using the H-E principles, 5. Integrated design review, 6. Why beyond engineering?, 7. Stakeholder analysis and mapping, 8. Cooperative game theory, 9. Social design principles, the S-principles, 10. Towards coalition building.

learning_objectives:
In this course students will learn the Building with Nature ecosystem-based design concept and its applications in water and coastal systems. More specifically, they will deepen their knowledge of hydraulic engineering principles (H), ecological principles (E) and social design principles (S) to develop more effective and sustainable nature based hydraulic infrastructure.

Learning objectives include:

1. Evaluate whether a hydraulic infrastructure is meeting engineering, ecosystem and societal goals

2. Evaluate the suitability of potential stakeholder coalitions for designing and implementing a particular Building with Nature project

3. Design a BwN solution for a coastal or riverine challenge based on engineering design principles, ecological design principles, and social design principles relevant to the Building with Nature approach.

These learning objectives clearly focus on designing nature based solutions in complex socio-technical systems, and on design for viable solutions in a multi-actor space. The additional complexity of taking interactions with and in the environment into account make this a challenging and relevant course.

course_name: Adaptive Planning for Management of Water Systems in Deltas
description:
Course will be offered if enough students enroll in this elective course. Minimum number of students: 10. Decision will be communicated in week 1.4.

This elective course will not be offered in the study year 2025-2026.

MSc Students that are looking for courses related to governance and water management, the course TPM803 Building with Nature offers a worthwhile alternative.  TPM803 will be taught in Q2.

Society is vulnerable to unexpected or difficult to predict events that can boost, but more often damage social and economic activities and/or the natural environment. Can we prepare for these events given that their frequency, scope, and impact are uncertain and that climate change exacerbates the uncertainties? What measures may we take "top down or bottom up" to protect the functionality, reliability, and/or the returns on investments of existing infrastructures and other built structures? And, while we plan for dealing with climate change (or other uncertain contextual factors such as the economy or political stability) what processes do we need to take into account in relation to the preferred locations for housing and production?

Researchers and policy-makers are deeply engaged with these questions. In this course we study their contributions with regard to coping with water-related, deeply uncertain events with large scale, uncertain impacts. Examples in this course will relate to floods, droughts and sea level rise.

You will delve into literature that helps you understand the concepts and tools that play a role in planning and decision-making under deep uncertainty. We will discuss how these tools differ from conventional planning methods and under what conditions they may be useful.

One important tool that is being introduced in the water-domain is the adaptation pathway. You will learn to develop "adaptation pathways". We will challenge you to critically reflect on the incentives that these pathways create for economic behavior. And you will learn how to set up an "implementation monitoring" plan that reflects the interests of the multiple stakeholders that are involved.
learning_objectives:
After taking this course students are able to:

1. Discuss important concepts - such as uncertainty, scenarios, options, system failure, tipping points, vulnerability, robustness, resilience, adaptive capacity, and adaptation - and explain how they are related

2. Articulate and analyse choices in long-term planning or decision-making under uncertainty

3. Apply a structured method to developing scenarios for plausible but uncertain futures

4. Design an adaptation pathway and evaluate its future performance from different stakeholder perspectives

5. Design a plan for monitoring of the implementation of adaptation pathways

6. Make recommendations on how to deal with the strengths and weaknesses of adaptation pathways during their implementation

LO5.4: Evaluate the performance of neural networks against simpler linear or tree-based models, and justify when a neural network might be the preferable approach, given data size and complexity.

Cross-validation

description:
The goal of the course is to get the students aquainted with the stochastic processes with `no' memory (Markov processes), where the probability of any future event only depends on the current state of the process. Such processes are Markov processes or Markov chains. Markov chains have many applications as statistical models of real-world processes. They provide the basis for general stochastic simulation methods known as Markov chain Monte Carlo, which are used for simulating sampling from complex probability distributions, and have found application in areas including Bayesian statistics, biology, chemistry, economics, finance, information theory, physics, signal processing, and speech processing.

Topics that will be covered include: discrete and continuous time Markov chains, transition matrix, classification of states, irreducibility and periodicity, invariant measure, return times and hitting times, long-term behavior of the system. Special Markov chains on countable state spaces: Branching processes, (survival vs extinction) Birth and death chains (recurrence, transience), Poisson point process. Random Walk on the integers Z and other graphs.

Moreover, the course will introduce Markov decision processes, which are a mathematical support tool for decision making under uncertainty. The mathematical concepts will be presented, and application of Markov decision processes to concrete decision contexts will be considered. Two real-life motivated decision making problems (in inventory management and replacement) will be modelled and solved with Markov decision processes.
learning_objectives:
(1) After the course, you are able to recognise a stochastic process as a Markov process by checking the Markov condition, and you are able to classify the states of a specific Markov processes,

(2) You are able to compute explicitly or numerically the invariant measure and hitting times of aperiodic, irreducible Markov chains on finite state-spaces using linear algebra.

(3) You are able to recognise and decide whether, in concrete examples, a birth and death chain is recurrent or transient and compute its invariant measure in the first case.

(4) You are able to prove that Simple Random Walk on Z and Z^2 is recurrent but transient on Z^3.

(5) You are able to use Poisson point processes as arrival times and can prove the relation to exponential inter-event times

(6) You are able to formulate a Markov reward process

(7) You are able to specify elements of Markov decision processes and apply a given Markov Decision Process to standard decision contexts

(8) You are able to, in a group setting, in a concrete modeling context, construct a Markov Decision Process model to solve a decision making problem

description:
The goal of inverse problems is to recover useful information about an unknown system or quantity from indirect and noisy measurements.

For example, a blurred and noisy image, such as one taken with an out-of-focus camera, contains only indirect information about the original scene. Recovering the sharp image from this measurement is a classic inverse problem.

Mathematically, image blur can be modelled as a convolution: the observed image is interpreted as a sharp image convolved with a kernel and corrupted by random noise. The corresponding inverse problem, recovering a sharp image from the blurred one, is called deconvolution. This inverse problem is ill-posed, meaning that the solution is highly sensitive to modelling errors and measurement noise. To obtain a stable and meaningful solution we can apply regularisation techniques.

Topics: Naïve inversion, (discrete) convolution, X-ray tomography, truncated singular value decomposition, Tikhonov and total variation regularisation, and short introduction to Bayesian approach to inverse problems.
learning_objectives:
After this course, you should be able to:

Model a measurement process as a matrix equation and identify when it leads to an ill-posed inverse problem.

Understand and explain why ill-posed problems require regularisation.

Design and implement a reconstruction method to recover an unknown quantity from indirect and noisy measurements.

Solve discrete inverse problems using MATLAB and present your results clearly in a written report.

3) Explain the implications of the mathematical results to the biological/physical system.

description: Finite differences, finite volumes in R^2, error analysis, discrete and continuous maximum principles, processing of boundary conditions, time integration.
learning_objectives:
The focus of this course is on two of the three most common discretization techniques: the finite difference method and the finite volume method. Before introducing, deriving, and applying these methods, we start with the theoretical principles of partial differential equations (PDEs) that are necessary to analyze PDEs before discretizing them. We then introduce the two discretization techniques. Additionally, we introduce iterative methods to solve nonlinear PDEs, and finally, we will examine various numerical time integration methods, which we introduce using the heat equation and the wave equation.

Specifically, by the end of the course, you should be able to:

1. Explain analytical properties of partial differential equations (PDEs) and the role of boundary and initial conditions that are important to obtain solutions to PDEs

2. Explain the properties, advantages and disadvantages of the finite difference method (FDM) and the finite volume method (FVM) to obtain approximate solutions to PDEs

3. Apply FDM and FVM to obtain approximate solutions to 1D and 2D systems of linear PDEs.

4. Apply two techniques to obtain solutions of non-linear PDEs, namely: the fixed-point scheme and Newtons method.

5. Implement numerical schemes for time-dependent PDE's on two specific equations: The diffusion and the wave equation.

6. Analyse the accuracy, stability, and convergence properties of all these above mentioned methods

This course provides an introduction to Fourier analysis for functions of one real variable.

The following topics are treated:

Fourier series of periodic functions that are absolutely integrable: basic properties, convergence results, and applications to partial differential equations (PDEs)

Fourier transform of absolute and square integrable functions: basic properties, inversion formulas, the Poisson summation formula, and the Shannon sampling theorem

Discrete Fourier transform (DFT): theory and computational aspects.
learning_objectives:
At the end of the course, you should be able to:

LO1) restate the definitions and give examples of the notions covered during the course

LO2) restate the statements of the results covered in the lectures and explain their proofs

LO3) apply the definitions together with the results treated during the course to solve new exercises.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description: Mathematics started with Euclid's elements some 2300 years ago. How did it lead up to the seven Millennium Prize problems that we face today, and why did it take 1800 years before people even invented the = sign? You would think that mathematical truths are absolute and indisputable, but the history of math is rife with controversies and debates. In this course you will see how mathematical concepts evolve over time, to give you a perspective on what you learn in our Delft BSc mathematics program.
learning_objectives: Understanding the evolution of analysis, geometry, logic, numerical mathematics, and statistics.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description: Modellen voor wiskundige vaardigheid, de rollen van de docent, didactische analyse van de leerstof, waaronder formuleren van leerdoelen en succescriteria, lesvoorbereiding, enkele (activerende) werkvormen, diagnostisch handelen, formatieve toetsing, observeren van lessen en geven van (delen van) lessen.
learning_objectives: De student kent de verschillende rollen van de docent en kan in een onderwijspraktijk invulling geven aan de rol van presentator, didacticus en afsluiter. De student kent de verschillende componenten van wiskundige vaardigheid en kan onderwijs voorbereiden dat die componenten bij lerenden ontwikkelt en kan daarbij gemaakte keuzen onderbouwen met theorie. De student kan minstens drie activerende werkvormen en een vorm van formatief handelen in praktijk brengen en daarbij gemaakte keuzen onderbouwen met theorie. De student kan lesmateriaal kritisch analyseren en aanpassen aan een onderwijspraktijk.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
Algorithms and data structures are fundamental notions in computer science. Understanding how they can be exploited in combination for better programming implementations in terms of time and space complexity is vital for writing efficient code. This course enables the student to:

Understand, explain, and implement standard data structures.

Understand, explain, and implement standard algorithms.

Apply standard data structures and algorithms to solve programming tasks.

Analyse and compare implementations with respect to their time and space complexity.

For any Computer Science students reading this, this course is not equivalent to CSE1305 nor equivalent to CSE2310. Although there is an overlap in topics (and course name), the focus of this course differs sufficiently and takes elements from both courses and is thus not a substitute for either. If you have passed both CSE1305 and CSE2310, then you can request an excemption for this course.
learning_objectives:
After this course, the student is able to:

LO-1 analyse the run time complexity of (recursive) (pseudo)code.

LO-2 analyse the space complexity of (recursive) (pseudo)code.

LO-3 analyse and implement (doubly) linked lists, arraylists, stacks, and queues.

LO-4 describe, analyse, and implement a variety of sorting algorithms (e.g., merge sort, quicksort).

LO-5 analyse and implement priorityqueues, heaps, and (search)trees.

LO-6 analyse and implement hash sets and maps.

LO-7 analyse and implement graph algorithms, such as: Breadth-First Search (BFS), Depth-First Search (DFS), Dijkstra, and PrimJarnik.

LO-8 design, implement, and analyse dynamic programming solutions for suitable problems.

LO-9 select the right datastructure and algorithm for a given problem with certain run time and memory requirements.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description: Het mentoraat is tijdens het 1e kwartaal met name bedoeld om je wegwijs te maken in het studeren van Technische Wiskunde aan de TU Delft. Vanaf kwartaal wordt de focus verlegd naar extra wiskundig inhoudelijke begeleiding. description:
Het doel van dit vak is tweeledig:

1) studenten kennis laten maken met verzamelingenleer, logica en bewijstechnieken

2) studenten laten oefenen met het aanpakken van wiskundige vraagstukken en het opschrijven van oplossingen / uitwerkingen.

Onderwerpen die behandeld zullen worden:

*predicatenlogica (proposities, connectieven, kwantoren, waarheidstabellen),

*bewijstechnieken (waaronder inductie en bewijs uit het ongerijmde),

*basale verzamelingenleer (bewerkingen op verzamelingen, kardinaliteit).

*relaties (waaronder ook functies, injectiviteit/surjectiviteit/bijectiviteit, equivalentierelaties).
learning_objectives:
De student kan eenvoudige bewijzen opstellen en op correctheid controleren.

De student kan van wiskundige uitspraken bepalen of ze waar of niet waar zijn.

De student kent de taal van de predicatenlogica en kan deze gebruiken om uitspraken te formuleren en te manipuleren.

De student kent en kan werken met elementaire concepten uit de verzamelingenleer, in het bijzonder operaties op verzamelingen, machtsverzamelingen, (equivalentie)relaties, functies en kardinaliteit.

De student kent enkele standaard bewijstechnieken en kan deze toepassen, in het bijzonder volledige inductie, bewijzen uit het ongerijmde, bewijzen door contrapositie.

De student kan in groepsverband een plan van aanpak formuleren om wiskundige problemen op te lossen.

description:
In dit vak leer je Calculus: Het deel van Analyse dat gaat over het daadwerkelijk uitrekenen van dingen.

In het bijzonder leer je limieten, afgeleides en integralen berekenen (deze laatste twee ook in meerdere dimensies), en gewone eerste-orde differentiaalvergelijkingen oplossen. Bovendien leer je rekenen met complexe getallen en vectoren.

In die zin kun je dit vak goed zien als een grote voortzetting van Wiskunde B van de middelbare school.

Natuurlijk zullen we ook uitleggen wat je nu aan het berekenen bent, maar precieze wiskundige definities en bewijzen zijn niet het (hoofd)doel van het vak; daarvoor zullen we vaak verwijzen naar Analyse 1. Voor vectoren doen we alleen het hoognodige, in het vak lineaire algebra gaat dat nog veel uitgebreider.
learning_objectives:
Na afloop van dit vak kun je

1. Functies inverteren en de afgeleides van inverses bepalen

2. Limieten en integralen berekenen met behulp van verschillende technieken

3. Gewone, eerste-orde differentiaalvergelijkingen en beginvoorwaarde-problemen oplossen, zowel numeriek als exact.

4. Rekenen met complexe getallen.

5. Rekenen met vectoren in ℝ^3.

6. Partiële afgeleides berekenen en ze toepassen in geschikte wiskundige problemen.

7. Meervoudige integralen bepalen, ook in pool-, cylinder- em bolcoördinaten.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
In dit vak leer je de basisconcepten van programmeren en pas je deze toe door zelf programma's te ontwikkelen in de programmeertaal Python.

In de colleges en daaraan gekoppelde practicumopdrachten komen de volgende onderwerpen aan de orde:

- De interactieve ontwikkelomgevingen Spyder.

- Interactief gebruik en "scripting".

- Variabelen en toekenningsopdrachten.

- Invoer en uitvoer via toetsenbord en beeldscherm.

- Datatypen integer, float en boolean.

- Scopes, name spaces en modules.

- Rekenkundige en logische expressies.

- Voorwaardelijke opdrachten.

- Strings, lists, tuples, dictionaries en sets.

- Indexering, mutable en immutable datatypen.

- Lus constructies.

- Definitie en aanroep van functies.

- Recursieve functies.

- Gebruik van modules en definitie van eigen modules.

- File input en output.

- Formatteren van data ten behoeve van uitvoer in tabelvorm.

- Gebruik van numpy, matplotlib en de datatypen array en matrix.

Deze onderwerpen zullen worden uitgelegd aan de hand van veelal wiskundige problemen. Ook in het practicum zullen de opdrachten vaak wiskundig van aard zijn.
learning_objectives:
Na afronding van dit vak moet je het volgende kunnen:

- een beschrijving van een eenvoudig probleem vertalen naar een algoritme.

- een eenvoudig algoritme implementeren in de programmeertaal Python en hierbij de volgende programmeertaalconstructies gebruiken: logische en rekenkundige expressies, toekenningsopdrachten, functies, voorwaardelijke opdrachten, lus-constructies, datastructuren met (geneste) lijsten en andere datatypen.

- programma's implementeren die invoer uit files lezen en uitvoer naar files schrijven.

- oplossingen van problemen definiëren met behulp van recursie en recursieve oplossingen implementeren.

- Python met behulp van de bibliotheken numpy en matplotlib gebruiken voor onder andere het oplossen van stelsels lineaire vergelijkingen en het plotten van grafieken.

- in programma's uitvoer in uitgelijnde kolommen formatteren om vervolgens in een file of op het beeldscherm te tonen.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description: This course is the first of a set of four mathematical modelling courses. These modelling courses teach how to use mathematical tools to analyse real-life problems. In this first course the modelling cycle is introduced and skills from calculus 1 and programming are used to define, analyse and improve mathematical models based on ODEs. The students also get an introduction into scientific literacy, writing and presenting.
learning_objectives:
By the end of the course, the student should be able to:
- apply the modelling cycle (problem definition - formulate mathematical model - calculations - validation) to an ordinary differential equation (ODE) problem
- write a computer program to solve the ODE numerically, perform numerical experiments and assess the outcomes
- work in a small group and efficiently interact with the colleague and supervisor.
- find and consult scientific literature related to the research project.
- present the work to her/his peers by means of a poster
- report their modeling outcomes in writing (using LaTeX)
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
This is an introduction to analysis for functions of one real variable.

The following topics are treated:

- sequences

- series

- continuity

- differentiation

- integration.
learning_objectives:
At the end of the course, you should be able to:

LO1) restate the definitions and give examples of the notions covered during the course

LO1.1: convergent, bounded, divergent and Cauchy sequence, subsequence, supremum, infimum, maximum, minimum, (strictly) monotone sequence, limes superior and inferior

LO1.2: convergent and absolutely convergent series

LO1.3: continuous, bounded and uniformly continuous function, continuous limit

description:
Vectoren zijn bekend: ze worden vaak gerepresenteerd als pijltjes die een grootte en richting aangeven en ze kunnen opgeteld en/of met een getal vermenigvuldigd worden.

Het vak lineaire algebra bestudeert vectoren. In eerste instantie wordt een andere representatie van pijltjes behandeld, waardoor het rekenen met vectoren eenvoudig wordt. Een van de voordelen van deze representatie is dat het algemener kan. Dit leidt tot de introductie van de vectorruimte R^n. Al snel zal gezien worden dat het nog algemener kan: functies bijvoorbeeld kunnen ook als vectoren gezien worden, en ook kan gerekend worden over bijvoorbeeld de complexe getallen. Het begrip vectorruimte beschrijft dit alles.

We zullen bestuderen wanneer en hoe vectorruimten (of deelruimten van vectorruimten) met eindig veel vectoren beschreven kunnnen worden. Centrale begrippen hierbij zijn onafhankelijkheid, basis en dimensie. Hét middel om hieraan te rekenen is het oplossen van stelsels lineaire vergelijkingen.

Aan de hand van de oplosmethode voor deze stelsels worden matrices geintroduceerd. Later zal blijken dat dit eigenlijk representaties zijn van zogenaamde lineaire afbeeldingen tussen eindig dimensionale vectorruimten. Nadat deze afbeeldingen geïntroduceerd zijn en we nagedacht hebben hoe we het beeld en eigenschappen als injectivieteit, surjectiviteit en inverteerbaarheid kunnen onderzoeken, zullen we zien hoe we met matrices kunnen gerekenen: optellen, scalair vermenigvuldigen, vermenigvuldigen en transponeren zijn operaties die je onder de knie moet gaan krijgen. Ook moet je weten wat het betekent dat matrices inverteerbaar zijn en hoe je de inverse van een matrix kunt berekenen en wat dit met de bijbehorende lineaire afbeelding te maken heeft.

De representatie van een lineaire afbeelding als matri hangt af van de basis die gekozen wordt voor het domein van de afbeelding. We zullen de verbanden tussen deze diverse representaties bestuderen. Deze hebben te maken met zogenaamde coordinatentransformaties.

Een ander begrip (dat zowel een meetkundige als algebraische interpretatie heeft) is de determinant van een vierkante matrix. Dit is bijvoorbeeld een maat voor de volumevergroting bij lineaire afbeeldingen, maar het geeft ook aan of een matrix (of lineaire afbeelding) inverteerbaar is of niet.

De cursus wordt geeindigd met de begrippen rang, kolomruimte, rijruimte en nulruimte van een matrix.

De lineaire algebra kent vele toepassingen zowel in de fundamentele wiskunde (algebra, kansrekening) als de toegepaste wiskunde (differntiaalvergelijkingen, numerieke wiskunde, statistiek, systeemtheorie) en natuurkunde (quantummechanica). Het is daarom een van de belangrijke basisvakken voor de opleiding.
learning_objectives:
Algemeen:

Aan het einde van de cursus zal de student:

wiskundige basisvaardigheden uit de lineaire algebra systematisch toe kunnen passen;

onderscheid kunnen maken tussen definities en stellingen en geleerd hebben hoe een wiskundige theorie is opgebouwd

eenvoudige bewijzen die betrekking hebben op lineaire algebra kunnen doorgronden, reproduceren en zelf maken;

1. Vectorruimten en deelruimten:

"vector, scalar, optelling, scalaire vermenigvuldiging, deelruimte, som, doorsnede, lineaire combinatie, lineair omhulsel (span), opspannen."

Weet hoe vectorruimten gedefinieerd worden, kan vectoren en scalairen uit elkaar houden, kent de vijf standaardvoorbeelden van vectorruimten en kan werken met de rekenregels. Kent de definitie van deelruimte van een vectorruimte, kan van verzamelingen in vectoruimten nagaan of het wel of geen deelruimte is en weet dat doorsnedes en sommen van deelruimten ook weer deelruimten zijn, net als de span van een aantal vectoren. Kan de juiste procedures kiezen die leiden tot antwoorden op vragen die te maken hebben met de begrippen lineaire combinatie en lineair omhulsel ('span') van vectoren en kan verschillende lineaire omhulsels relateren.

2. Oplossen van stelsels lineaire vergelijkingen

"Coëfficiënten- en aangevulde matrix, elementaire rijoperaties, (gereduceerde) echelonvorm, pivot, rijreductie (vegen), Gauss-Jordan-eliminatie, vrije variabelen, consistente en inconsistente stelsels."

Kan op een efficiënte en overzichtelijke manier met behulp van (gereduceerde) echelonvormen bepalen hoeveel oplossingen een stelsel (eventueel met parameters) heeft en kan, indien nodig, alle oplossingen bepalen. Hierbij gebruikt de student de juiste terminologie.

3. (On)afhankelijkheid, basis en dimensie:

"(On)afhankelijkheid, basis, uitdunningsstelling, uitbreidingsstelling, unieke representatiestelling."

Herkent of vectoren afhankelijk dan wel onafhankelijk zijn, kan deze begrippen omschrijven en gebruiken bij afleidingen. Kan bases voor en de dimensie van een gegeven deelruimte bepalen en kan nagaan of een stel vectoren een basis vormt voor een gegeven deelruimte. Weet bases en dimensie en hun eigenschappen toe te passen in afleidingen.

4. Lineaire afbeeldingen:

"Functie, domein, codomein, beeld (bereik), lineaire afbeelding, nulafbeelding, identieke afbeelding, spiegeling, rotatie, projectie, matrixtransformatie, matrixrepresentatie, compositie, inverteerbaarheid, kern en beeld, nullity en rang."

Weet hoe functies gedefinieerd worden, kan lineaire afbeeldingen omschrijven, herkennen en voorbeelden geven. Kan eigenschappen van lineaire afbeeldingen gebruiken bij afleidingen Kan nagaan of een lineaire afbeelding injectief, surjectief en/of inverteerbaar is en kan de inverse afbeelding uitrekenen. Kan uitleggen wat de kern en het beeld van een lineaire afbeelding zijn en kan deze voor een gegeven lineaire afbeelding bepalen. Kan matrixrepresentaties tov verschillende bases berekenen.

5. Matrixalgebra:

Matrix, rijen, kolommen, afmeting, nulmatrix, vierkante matrix, diagonaalmatrix, eenheidsmatrix, driehoeksmatrix, symmetrische matrix, inverteerbare matrix, optellen, scalair vermenigvuldigen, vermenigvuldigen, transponeren, inverteren, rekenregels.""

Weet wat matrices zijn, kan ze onderscheiden van vectoren en scalairen en kan diverse soorten matrices benoemen, kent de algebraïsche operaties voor matrices met de bijbehorende rekenregels en eigenschappen en kan berekeningen met matrices op zo efficiënt mogelijke manier uitvoeren en redeneringen met matrices in afleidingen gebruiken.

6. Coördinatentransformaties:

"coördinatisering, coördinatentransformatie."

Kan, via coördinatentransformaties, aangeven hoe de diverse matrixrepresentaties van lineaire afbeeldingen in het eindig dimensionale geval samenhangen.

7. Determinanten (en uitwendig product):

"Determinant, cofactorontbinding, ontwikkelen naar rij of kolom, uitwendig product, oppervlakte parallellogram, inhoud parallellepipedum."

Kan determinanten uitrekenen via een combinatie van het veegproces en cofactorontbinding en weet dat in dit geval ook met kolommen geveegd mag worden. Kent de rekenregels van een determinant en kan die op de juiste manier gebruiken. (Kan de oppervlakte van een parallellogram en de inhoud van een parallellepipedum met behulp van determinanten bepalen. Kent de definitie en eigenschappen van het uitwendig product tussen twee vectoren uit R^3 en kan dit uitrekenen.)
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
Deze cursus geeft een introductie in discrete wiskunde. We bestuderen 'discrete objecten' zoals gehele getallen, verzamelingen en grafen. Voorbeelden van grafen zijn sociale netwerken of wegennetwerken.

In de eerste helft van de cursus verdiepen we ons in verschillende telprincipes, zoals binomiale en multinomiale coëfficiënten, dubbeltellen, inclusie-exclusie en recurrente betrekkingen. We behandelen ook eigenschappen van de gehele getallen zoals modulo-rekenen en de uniciteit van de priemontbinding.

In de tweede helft van de cursus verkennen we basisbegrippen van de grafentheorie zoals Euleriaanse wandelingen, bomen, matching, planaire grafen en graafkleuring.

Gedurende de cursus wordt ook nadruk gelegd op het toepassen van 'discreet denken' om problemen op te lossen en op algorithmische aspecten, waaronder het algoritme van Euclides, breadth-first search, bipartiet matching en greedy algoritmen.
learning_objectives:
1) Formuleren van rigoreuze wiskundige bewijzen.

2) Oplossen van telproblemen met behulp van technieken zoals dubbeltellen, binomiaalcoëfficiënten, bijecties, inclusie-exclusie en recursieve betrekkingen

3) Formuleren van definities en stellingen en uitleggen van de bijbehorende bewijzen

4) Bewijzen van nieuwe wiskundige resultaten door concepten, voorbeelden en stellingen uit het vak te combineren

5) Toepassen van algoritmen uit het vak zoals het algoritme van Euclides om de grootste gemene deler te vinden, augmenting paths of een maximum matching te vinden en boomalgoritmen zoals depth-first search.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
Het volgende materiaal wordt behandeld.

*Dictaat "Analysis 1" van Jan van Neerven: Secties 6.1, 6.2, 6.3, 6.4.

*Boek van Lax en Terrell: Secties 2.1, 2.2, 3.5, het deel van 6.6 over de transformatiestelling, 7.1, 7.2, 7.3, 8.1, 8.2, 8.3.

Concreet betreft dit de volgende onderwerpen. Op analytisch niveau, dat wil zeggen dat studenten de bewijzen begrijpen en de theorie kunnen toepassen, behandelen we:

*Machtreeksen

*De exponentiele functie

*Het logaritme

*Trigonometrische functies

*Functies van meerdere variabelen, vectorvelden, krommen

*Gesloten en open deelverzamelingen van R^n, continuiteit, limieten van functies van meerdere variabelen.

Dit materiaal komt zowel uit het diktaat als het boek.

De volgende onderwerpen worden behandeld op een calculus niveau. Dit betekent dat studenten in staat moeten zijn het materiaal toe te passen (typisch om integralen uit te rekenen) en de concepten die worden behandeld moeten begrijpen en kunnen interpreteren. Het is echter niet nodig de bewijzen van de stellingen te kennen.

*Gradient, divergentie, rotatie

*Substitutieregel voor functies van meerdere veranderlijken (wordt eventueel beperkt tot 2 of 3 variabelen).

*Lijnintegralen.

*Conservatieve vectorvelden

*Oppervlakteintegralen

*Stellingen van Green, Stokes en Gauss (divergentiestelling).
learning_objectives:
*De student is in staat om de theorie van machtreeksen te analyseren en toe te passen.

*De student is in staat om de exponentiële functie te analyseren en toe te passen.

*De student is in staat om de logaritme te analyseren en toe te passen.

*De student is in staat om de basis goniometrische functies te analyseren en toe te passen.

*De student is in staat om de theorie van functies van meerdere variabelen, vectorvelden en krommen te analyseren en toe te passen.

*De student is in staat om gesloten en open deelverzamelingen van R^n, continuïteit en limieten van functies van meerdere variabelen te analyseren.

*De student kan de gradiënt, divergentie en rotatie toepassen en deze berekenen voor concrete functies.

*De student kan de substitutieregel en variabelenwisseling toepassen om integralen van functies van meerdere variabelen te berekenen.

*De student begrijpt wat lijnintegralen zijn en kan deze toepassen om de lijnintegraal van concrete functies en vectorvelden te bepalen.

*De student begrijpt wat een conservatief vectorveld is en kan dit toepassen om integralen over gesloten paden te bepalen.

*De student kan oppervlakte-integralen toepassen om de integralen van functies en vectorvelden over oppervlakken te berekenen

*De student kan de stellingen van Green, Stokes en Gauss (ook bekend als de divergentiestelling) toepassen om integralen van concrete functies en vectorvelden te berekenen.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
This is the second half of the course covering fundamental aspects of Linear Algebra in BSc applied mathematics program (first year). Specifically, this course deals with the following topics:

+ Spectral analysis: eigenvectors and generalized eigenvectors of linear operators, eigenvalue decomposition (diagonalization) and the Jordan canonical form of a linear operator.

+ Orthogonalization: Inner products, adjoints, orthogonal projections, orthogonal bases and their properties, Gram-Schmidt procedure.

+ Optimization: least squares, quadratic forms and constrained quadratic optimization.

+ Singular value decomposition, low-rank approximations, pseudo inverses.

+ Computational aspects of the above concepts.

The topics covered are important for many fields in applied mathematics, including differential equations, data science, and numerical analysis.
learning_objectives:
At the end of the course, the student will be able to:

1. Perform spectral analysis and diagonalization of linear operators using the notion of eigenvalues, eigenvectors and Jordan canonical forms.

2. Construct orthogonal bases for inner product spaces using the Gram-Schmidt procedure.

3. Solve optimization problems such as unconstrained least squares using adjoints and constrained quadratic optimization problems using orthogonal diagonalization of quadratic forms.

4. Compute pseudo-inverses and low-rank approximations of a linear transformation using the notion of singular value decomposition (SVD).

5. Explain the numerical and computational aspects of the above mathematical concepts.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description: Deze cursus is de tweede van een rij van vier vakken wiskundig modelleren. In deze modelleervakken leert de student om wiskundig gereedschap te gebruiken voor relevante praktijkproblemen. In dit tweede vak gebruiken de studenten de modelleercyclus om optimalisatieproblemen op te lossen. De studenten moeten daarbij programmeren, verder oefenen in wetenschappelijk schrijven en presenteren. Daarnaast leren de studenten teamworkvaardigheden.
learning_objectives:
Aan het eind van de cursus, kan de student:

De modelleercyclus (probleemdefinitie - een wiskundig model formuleren - berekeningen - validatie) gebruiken voor een optimalisatieprobleem.

description: This course is about ordinary differential equations (ODE). For first order ODE we will treat linear, separable, and exact equations. We will prove existence and uniqueness of solutions, using Picard iterations. For second order ODE we will introduce the concepts of a Wronskian and a fundamental solution, as well as introduce the method of reduction of order. We will learn how to solve constant coefficient linear ODEs using the methods of variation of parameters and judicious guessing for finding particular solutions. Moreover, we will treat power series solutions, the method of Frobenius for equations with singular points and the method of solving ODE using the Laplace transform. We will treat higher order ODE as well as systems of linear ODE, using the eigenvalue-eigenvector method for finding solutions. We will also cover qualitative theory of ODE, in particular stability of solutions and equilibria, invariant sets, the Hartman-Grobman linearisation theorem and phase portraits of linear systems.
learning_objectives:
After successfully completing the course, you will be able to use the theory of ordinary differential equations (ODEs) to solve or perform qualitative analysis on (systems of) differential equations. In particular, you can

1) solve linear (systems of) ODEs

2) solve separable ODEs and exact ODEs

3) determine the stability of solutions of ODEs

4) use theorems and techniques introduced in the course to prove properties such as local existence and uniqueness of solutions.

5) Use ideas and techniques from the proofs in the course to prove related results.

6) solve second order ODEs using power series and Frobenius theory.

7) determine periodic or asymptotic behaviour of solutions of ODEs.

8) sketch the phase planes of nonlinear systems of ODEs.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
Doel van het vak is inzicht en begrip te ontwikkelen voor structuren waar onzekerheid een rol speelt. Je maakt je basisvaardigheden in de kansrekening eigen. Onderwerpen die aan bod komen zijn:

1. Elementaire kansberekening en combinatoriek.

2. Discrete en continue stochasten. Belangrijke discrete en continue verdelingen en de context waarin ze gebruikt worden.

3. Verwachting, variantie en momentgenererende functie.

4. Meerdimensionale stochasten, onafhankelijke stochasten, covariantie, conditionele kansdichtheid en verwachting.

5. Ongelijkheid van Markov en Chebyshev.

6. Convergentie in kans en de wet van de grote aantallen.

7. Convergentie in verdeling en de centrale limietstelling.
learning_objectives:
Na het succesvol afronden van dit vak kun je:

1. basisregels uit de kansrekening toepassen zoals de totale kanswet, de regel van Bayes en regels voor onafhankelijke gebeurtenissen.

2. berekeningen maken met discrete en continue stochasten, zoals het uitrekenen van de verwachting, variantie, momentgenererende functie en de verdeling van getransformeerde stochasten.

3. in concrete modelleringscontext de juiste kansverdeling toepassen.

4. verwachtingen, marginale verdelingen, en conditionele verdelingen uitrekenen voor meerdimensionale stochasten, en het begrip covariantie toepassen in connectie met onafhankelijkheid.

5. de ongelijkheden van Markov en Chebyshev toepassen, waaronder voor het bewijzen dat een rij stochasten convergeert.

6. de wet van de grote aantallen en centrale limietstelling toepassen en bewijzen, ook in licht aangepaste context (bijvoorbeeld met zwakke afhankelijkheid of ongelijke verdelingen).
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

description:
This course offers a rigorous introduction to analysis in metric spaces, a framework that extends the familiar geometry of Euclidean space to far more general settings with applications accross various fields of mathematics. Typical examples are:

The space of continuous functions (Differential equations)

The space of square integrable functions (Partial differential equations, Numerical analysis, Probability theory, Quantum mechanics, Graph theory, etc.)

The space of summable sequences (Machine learning)

Topics treated during the course include:

Cauchy and convergent sequences

Open and closed sets

(Uniform) continuity and homeomorphisms

Total boundedness

Completeness and fixed points

Compactness

Uniform convergence

All discussed topics culminate in a discussion of Fourier series for periodic continuous functions.
learning_objectives:
At the end of the course, you should be able to write rigorous mathematical proofs in the context of metric spaces. In particular, you should be able to:

Formulate the definition of the main notions of the theory of metric spaces and explain the connection to their counterparts in the real number line.

Prove and apply the characterizations of convergent sequences, open and closed sets and continuous functions treated during the course.

Prove and apply completeness, for example to show existence of fixed points.

Use the definitions of totally bounded and compact metric spaces to prove properties of such spaces.

Relate pointwise and uniform convergence to the metric space of bounded functions and show results for sequences of bounded (continuous) functions.

Study periodic continuous functions using their Fourier coefficients.
faculty: Electrical Engineering, Mathematics and Computer Science

The students are able to execute basic algorithms for solving linear programming, integer linear programming and nonlinear programming problems, to understand the outcomes of the algorithms and to apply duality.

The students know basic theorems of linear and nonlinear optimization and are able to prove variations of these theorems.

The students can apply basic algorithms for network optimization problems (shortest path, max flow, travelling salesman problem).

The students are able to design reductions between optimization problems and to prove correctness of those reductions.
